{
  "abstract_verbatim": "For every prime <i>p</i> ≥ 5, we construct an explicit eight-stage filtration of $`L_2L_{K(3)}\\mathbb S_p^\\wedge`$ by the local-sphere layers in the height-three chromatic-splitting pattern. The map from its first stage to the overlap is the canonical unit, and two signed fracture formulas identify all attachments for the chosen local maps and compatibility homotopy. A companion canonical-map theorem further implies that the first height-one attachment is nonzero.",

<a id="pm-s1"></a>
## 1. Abstract and result contract

> For every prime <i>p</i> ≥ 5, we construct an explicit eight-stage filtration of $`L_2L_{K(3)}\mathbb S_p^\wedge`$ by the local-sphere layers in the height-three chromatic-splitting pattern. The map from its first stage to the overlap is the canonical unit, and two signed fracture formulas identify all attachments for the chosen local maps and compatibility homotopy. A companion canonical-map theorem further implies that the first height-one attachment is nonzero.

- **claim-canonical-unit-filtration** (construction, [source](#stmt-thm-main)): For every prime $p\geq5$, there are $E(2)$-local $S$-modules and maps $$0=F_0\longrightarrow F_1\longrightarrow\cdots\longrightarrow F_8, \qquad e:F_8\xrightarrow{\simeq}X,$$ whose successive cofibers $C_i=\mathop{\mathrm{cofib}}(F_{i-1}\to F_i)$, in order, are $$\begin{array}{c\|l@{\qquad\qquad}c\|l} i&C_i&i&C_i\\ \hline 1&L_2S&5&\Sigma^{-5}H\mathbb Q_p\\ 2&\Sigma^{-1}L_2S&6&\Sigma^{-6}H\mathbb Q_p\\ 3&\Sigma^{-3}L_1S&7&\Sigma^{-8}H\mathbb Q_p\\ 4&\Sigma^{-4}L_1S&8&\Sigma^{-9}H\mathbb Q_p. \end{array}$$ Under $F_1\simeq L_2S$, the composite $F_1\to F_8\xrightarrow e X$ is the canonical map $L_2(S\to L_{K(3)}S)$.
  - Explanation: Constructs the ordered local-sphere filtration of the height-three overlap and identifies its first map with the canonical unit.
- **claim-localization-boundary** (theorem, [source](#stmt-lem-boundary)): Let $a:A\to B$ be a map in a stable category, and let $L$ be an exact localization for which $La$ is an equivalence. Choose an inverse of $La$ and its inverse homotopies, and put $$\tau:B\longrightarrow LB\xrightarrow{(La)^{-1}}LA,\qquad N=\mathop{\mathrm{fib}}(A\longrightarrow LA).$$ The inverse homotopy makes $\tau$ a map under $A$, and therefore gives $$\bar\tau:\mathop{\mathrm{cofib}}(a)\longrightarrow\mathop{\mathrm{cofib}}(A\to LA) \simeq\Sigma N.$$ If $i:N\to A$ is the fiber inclusion, then the connecting map of the cofiber sequence of $a$ is $$\label{eq:boundary-lemma} \partial_a=(-\Sigma i)\bar\tau.$$ If $M$ is another exact localization and $N$ is $M$-local, the middle cofiber can equivalently be written $\mathop{\mathrm{cofib}}(MA\to MLA)$, using its localization identification.
  - Explanation: Expresses the connecting map through the localization fiber with the prescribed negative rotation sign and coherent inverse data.
- **claim-ordered-fracture-construction** (construction, [source](#stmt-prop-fracture)): Let $X$ be an $E(2)$-local $S$-module. Suppose the following module maps and homotopies are given.* 1. *A map $w:W\to X$ for which $L_{K(2)}w$ is an equivalence. Put $Y=\mathop{\mathrm{cofib}}(w)$, with quotient $q:X\to Y$.* 2. *An equivalence $\kappa:L_{K(1)}U_{\mathrm{mid}}\xrightarrow{\simeq}L_{K(1)}Y$, a rational map $r:L_0U_{\mathrm{mid}}\to L_0Y$, and a specified homotopy of $Q$-module maps between $$\label{eq:compatibility} \begin{gathered} L_0U_{\mathrm{mid}}\longrightarrow L_0L_{K(1)}U_{\mathrm{mid}} \xrightarrow{L_0\kappa}L_0L_{K(1)}Y,\\ L_0U_{\mathrm{mid}}\xrightarrow rL_0Y\longrightarrow L_0L_{K(1)}Y. \end{gathered}$$* 3. *A map $b:V\to L_0X$ for which $$\label{eq:quotient-basis} t_0:V\xrightarrow bL_0X\xrightarrow{L_0q}L_0Y \longrightarrow\mathop{\mathrm{cofib}}(r)$$ is an equivalence.* *Then there is a filtration in $E(2)$-local $S$-modules $$0=F_0\longrightarrow F_1\longrightarrow\cdots\longrightarrow F_8 \xrightarrow[\simeq]{e}X$$ with ordered cofibers $W_1,W_2,U_3,U_4,V_5,V_6,V_7,V_8$. The composite $F_2=W\to F_8\xrightarrow eX$ is $w$.
  - Explanation: Assembles the filtration from a localized equivalence, compatible middle maps, and an equivalence onto the rational quotient.
- **claim-signed-attachment-identification** (theorem, [source](#stmt-thm-attachment-identification)): Fix the data $w,\kappa,r,b$ and the compatibility homotopy of [prop:fracture](#prop:fracture). Choose coherent inverse data for $L_{K(2)}w$, and carry out that proposition’s construction. Use exactly its fracture map $h$, pullback stages $F_i$, projection $a:F_4\to X$, quotient $Z=\mathop{\mathrm{cofib}}(a)$, equivalence $t=\widetilde z b:V\xrightarrow{\simeq}Z$, and terminal projection $e:F_8\to X$, choosing the coherent inverse data for $L_Ja$ at the indicated step. Under the resulting ordered cofiber identifications $$W_1,\ W_2,\ U_3,\ U_4,\ V_5,\ V_6,\ V_7,\ V_8,$$ the connecting maps of this same filtration are $$\begin{gathered} \partial_1=0,\qquad \partial_2=0,\qquad \partial_3=d_3,\qquad \partial_4=\Sigma(F_2\to F_3)d_4,\\ \partial_i=\Sigma(F_4\to F_{i-1})g_i \qquad(5\leq i\leq8), \end{gathered}$$ where $d=\partial_wh$, $g=\partial_at$, $d_i=d\|_{U_i}$, and $g_i=g\|_{V_i}$. The maps $d$ and $g$ are the signed roofs $$\begin{aligned} d:\ U_{\mathrm{mid}}\xrightarrow hY\xrightarrow{\bar\tau_2} &\mathop{\mathrm{cofib}}(L_1W\longrightarrow L_1L_{K(2)}W)\\ &\simeq\Sigma\mathop{\mathrm{fib}}(W\longrightarrow L_{K(2)}W) \xrightarrow{-\Sigma j_W}\Sigma W, \end{aligned}$$ and $$\begin{aligned} g:\ V\xrightarrow bL_0X\longrightarrow L_0L_JX &\xrightarrow{(L_0L_Ja)^{-1}}L_0L_JF_4\\ &\longrightarrow\mathop{\mathrm{cofib}}(L_0F_4\longrightarrow L_0L_JF_4)\\ &\simeq\Sigma\mathop{\mathrm{fib}}(F_4\longrightarrow L_JF_4) \xrightarrow{-\Sigma j_a}\Sigma F_4. \end{aligned}$$ Here $\bar\tau_2,j_W,j_a$ are the maps defined from the same construction and inverse data above.
  - Explanation: Identifies every connecting map of the same chosen filtration by the signed fracture roofs.
- **claim-stabilizer-resolutions** (theorem, [source](#stmt-h3-lem-framework-groups)): The compact groups $P_3,H,P_2,P_1,\mathop{\mathrm{GL}}_2(\mathbb Z_p)$ and $\mathop{\mathrm{SL}}_2(\mathbb Z_p)$ have no elements of order $p$. Their $p$-cohomological dimensions are respectively $9,8,4,1,4,3$. Their adjoint orientation characters are trivial. Their trivial $\mathbb Z_p$-modules admit finite resolutions by finitely generated projective completed group-ring modules.
  - Explanation: Establishes absence of prime torsion, the stated cohomological dimensions, trivial orientation characters, and finite projective resolutions for the listed groups.
- **claim-semilinear-descent** (theorem, [source](#stmt-h3-lem-framework-semilinear)): Let $k'/k$ be a finite extension of finite fields with Galois group $\Gamma$. On $W(k')$-modules carrying a semilinear $\Gamma$-action, the invariants functor is exact. The same assertion holds for reductions modulo $p^\ell$, and the associated finite-group higher cohomology vanishes. These assertions respect continuous equivariant maps.
  - Explanation: Makes semilinear finite-field invariants exact, including finite Witt reductions and continuous equivariant maps.
- **claim-regular-torsion-levels** (construction, [source](#stmt-h3-geom-regular-levels)): For $l\geq1$, form the reduced closure of the locus of $r$ points of $\mathcal G[p^l]$ whose images are a basis of the étale quotient at the generic point of $A_m$. Its coordinate algebra $B_l$ is finite over $A_m$, and its lifted point coordinates $t_{1,l},\ldots,t_{r,l}$ give isomorphisms $$B_l=k[[t_{1,l},\ldots,t_{r,l}]],\qquad C_l:=A_m[t_{1,l}^{p^{ml}},\ldots,t_{r,l}^{p^{ml}}] =k[[t_{1,l}^{p^{ml}},\ldots,t_{r,l}^{p^{ml}}]].$$ The subalgebra on the left is already complete. The algebra $C_l[u_m^{-1}]$ is the finite étale algebra of bases of $\mathcal G^{\mathrm{et}}[p^l]$ over $A_m[u_m^{-1}]$. Over this basis cover, $B_l[u_m^{-1}]$ is the algebra of all generator lifts, without taking a reduction. The transition maps $B_j\to B_l$, $j\leq l$, are finite injective maps, and $$t_{i,j}\in k[[t_{1,l}^{p^{m(l-j)}},\ldots,t_{r,l}^{p^{m(l-j)}}]].$$
  - Explanation: Identifies the finite basis and lift algebras as power-series rings while retaining the entire infinitesimal lift scheme and its transitions.
- **claim-universal-cover-coordinates** (construction, [source](#stmt-h3-geom-universal-cover)): Let $(R,R^+)$ be an affinoid perfectoid $k$-algebra and specialize the parameters of $A_m$ to $R^{\circ\circ}$. For the resulting formal law $\mathcal G_a$, there is a natural additive isomorphism $$H_3(R)\ \xrightarrow{\ \Phi_a\ }\ \varprojlim_{[p]}\mathcal G_a(R^{\circ\circ}).$$ Writing $P_a=[p]_{\mathcal G_a}$, its coordinates and inverse are $$\label{h3:geom:cover-formulas} \Phi_a(z)_j=\lim_{n\to\infty} P_a^{\circ n}\bigl(z^{1/p^{3(j+n)}}\bigr),\qquad \Phi_a^{-1}((t_j))=\lim_{j\to\infty}t_j^{p^{3j}}.$$ These formulas commute with change of coefficients and with changes of deformation framing. Over an algebraically closed perfectoid field, the kernel of the zeroth projection is the integral Tate module of the étale quotient of $\mathcal G_a$.
  - Explanation: Gives mutually inverse limiting coordinates for the Honda universal cover and identifies the Tate-module kernel over an algebraically closed perfectoid field.
- **claim-completed-coordinate-comparison** (theorem, [source](#stmt-h3-thm-coordinate-comparison)): There is a natural $P_3\times\mathop{\mathrm{GL}}_r(\mathbb Z_p)$-equivariant isomorphism $$\mathcal T_m\ \simeq\ (H_3^r)_{\mathrm{ind}}.$$ The map takes a compatible basis of generator lifts to $z_i=\lim_l t_{i,l}^{p^{3l}}$. It identifies the relevant completed function algebras with their spectral norms on exhausted closed smaller balls. The assertion holds on the relative perfectoid site and remains valid after adjoining arbitrary profinite parameters.
  - Explanation: Identifies the completed Tate-basis tower with independent Honda tuples, equivariantly and with spectral norms and profinite parameters.
- **claim-relative-curve-sections** (theorem, [source](#stmt-h3-geom-curve-inputs)): There are natural isomorphisms of additive sheaves $$H_s\simeq\bigl(S\longmapsto H^0(X_S,V_s)\bigr).$$ The automorphism sheaf of $V_s$ is the locally profinite group $D_s^{\times}$. A family fiberwise isomorphic to $V_s$ is locally of that form for the pro-étale topology. If $\tau$ denotes the morphism of v-sites associated with $X_S$, then $$R\tau_*\mathcal O^a=\underline{\mathbb Q_p}^{\,a},\qquad R\tau_*E=\tau_*E[0]$$ for every family $E$ fiberwise isomorphic to a $V_s$. Relative sections are fully faithful on $\mathbb Q_p$-linear sheaf morphisms between these bundles and slope-zero bundles. All assertions commute with base change and v-descent.
  - Explanation: Identifies Honda section sheaves, automorphism groups, local bundle forms, relative vanishing, and full faithfulness under base change.
- **claim-independent-extension-locus** (classification, [source](#stmt-h3-geom-independent-extensions)): Independent sections of $V_3$ define a subbundle $\mathcal O^r\hookrightarrow V_3$ with quotient fiberwise $V_m$. Conversely, an extension of $V_m$ by $\mathcal O^r$ has middle bundle fiberwise $V_3$ if and only if its class lies in $\mathcal E_m$.
  - Explanation: Characterizes independent sections and independent extension classes by the required basic middle bundle and quotient.
- **claim-integral-frame-comparison** (construction, [source](#stmt-h3-prop-integral-frames)): Put $\mathcal Y_m=[\mathcal X_m/P_3]$. There is an equivalence of v-stacks over $k$ $$\label{h3:geom:frame-stack} \mathcal Y_m\simeq [\mathcal E_m/(\mathop{\mathrm{GL}}_r(\mathbb Z_p)\times P_m)].$$ It carries an actual universal sequence $$\label{h3:geom:universal-sequence} 0\longrightarrow\mathcal L_r\otimes_{\mathbb Z_p}\mathcal O \longrightarrow\mathcal V_3 \longrightarrow\mathcal V_m\longrightarrow0,$$ where $\mathcal L_r$ is the integral étale Tate local system and $\mathcal V_s$ are $P_s$-structured forms. The two presentations give the classifying maps to $BP_3$, $B\mathop{\mathrm{GL}}_r(\mathbb Z_p)$ and $BP_m$, and their determinant characters satisfy $$\label{h3:geom:determinant-product} \mathop{\mathrm{Nrd}}_3=\det_{\mathop{\mathrm{GL}}_r}\,\mathop{\mathrm{Nrd}}_m.$$ With the convention $(A,b)e=A_*((b^{-1})^*e)$ for extension classes, the kernel scalar $u$ acts on $N_m^r$ by $u$ and the quotient scalar $u$ by $u^{-1}$.* *For $m=2$, let $\widetilde{\mathcal X}_2$ be the full connected-marking tower. It admits a normalized integral étale generator, fixed by $H=\ker(\mathop{\mathrm{Nrd}}:P_3\to\mathbb Z_p^\times)$. There are compatible equivalences $$\label{h3:geom:normalized-tower} \widetilde{\mathcal X}_2\simeq\operatorname{Surj}(V_3,V_2), \qquad [\widetilde{\mathcal X}_2/H]\simeq N_2^*.$$ The full residual norm quotient acts in the second equivalence by scalar units, in the kernel convention just specified. No section of $P_3\to\mathbb Z_p^\times$ is involved.
  - Explanation: Constructs the frame-stack equivalence, universal sequence, determinant identity, scalar conventions, and normalized coheight-one marking tower.
- **claim-uniform-etale-sections** (theorem, [source](#stmt-h3-geom-uniform-etale-descent)): Let $L=\mathop{\mathrm{colim}}_i B_i$ be an injective union of finite étale $K$-algebras, with their maximum valuation norms, and put $C=\widehat{L^{\mathrm{perf}}}$. For every finite étale $L$-algebra $E$, the map $$\mathop{\mathrm{Hom}}_{L\text{-alg}}(E,L)\longrightarrow \mathop{\mathrm{Hom}}_{L\text{-alg}}(E,C)$$ is bijective. Each section on the right is defined at one finite separable stage $B_j$, even if the numbers of field factors in the $B_i$ are unbounded.
  - Explanation: Descends finite étale sections from completed perfection to a common finite separable stage even when later products have unboundedly many factors.
- **claim-normalized-marking-descent** (construction, [source](#stmt-h3-lem-marking-descent)): The normalized étale generator of [h3:prop:integral-frames](#h3:prop:integral-frames) descends to a compatible integral marking over $L$. It is $H$-invariant, and the full $P_3$ action changes it by the constant unit $\mathop{\mathrm{Nrd}}(g)$, up to the common inverse convention. At level $l$, the torsor of its lifts to $\mathcal G[p^l]$ has coordinate algebra $$\label{h3:geom:height-two-roots} L^{1/p^{2l}}.$$ The connected marking makes this a torsor for $\Gamma_2[p^l]_L$. The group $H$ acts trivially on the translation group, while $P_2$ acts by constant Honda automorphisms.* *For a finite connected-marking level $B=L^\Pi$, with $\Pi\subset P_2$ open, put $B^{\mathrm b}=\widehat{B^{\mathrm{perf}}}$; the superscript here denotes completed perfection, not tilting. There is a pro-étale $\Pi$-torsor $$\label{h3:geom:completed-level-torsor} \operatorname{Spa}(L^{\mathrm c})\longrightarrow \operatorname{Spa}(B^{\mathrm b}),$$ and consequently $$\label{h3:geom:finite-level-stack} [\operatorname{Spa}(B^{\mathrm b})/H]\simeq[N_2^*/\Pi].$$ These equivalences are natural under level changes and after extension to an algebraically closed perfectoid base.
  - Explanation: Descends the normalized marking, identifies its root torsors and residual actions, and constructs the finite-level completed quotient-stack comparison.
- **claim-invariant-differential** (construction, [source](#stmt-h3-lem-invariant-differential)): There is an equivariant isomorphism $$\label{h3:geom:canonical-lines} \bigwedge^2\Omega^1_{A/k,\mathrm{cts}}\simeq\omega^3[\det], \qquad \Omega^1_{K/k}\simeq\omega_K^{p+2}[\det].$$ Here $\det$ is the reduced norm character of $P_3$. The connected marking over $L$ supplies a generator $U_0$ of $\omega_L$ fixed by $P_3$. Consequently <a href="#h3:geom:canonical-lines" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="h3:geom:canonical-lines">[h3:geom:canonical-lines]</a> gives a nonzero differential $\eta\in\Omega^1_{L/k}$ fixed by $H$, defined at a finite separable marking level. Changes of the connected marking act on these frames by their constant cotangent characters.
  - Explanation: Identifies canonical differential lines and obtains a nonzero differential fixed by the norm kernel at a finite separable marking stage.
- **claim-ordinary-root-torsor** (construction, [source](#stmt-h3-lem-ordinary-torsor)): Let $B_0=A[x^{-1}]$. The ordinary connected–étale sequence of $\mathcal G$ over $B_0$ is $$0\longrightarrow\mathcal C\longrightarrow\mathcal G \longrightarrow\mathcal E\longrightarrow0,$$ where $\mathcal C$ has height one and is of multiplicative type, and $\mathcal E$ is étale of height two. For every $l\geq1$, the scheme of splittings of its $p^l$-torsion sequence is canonically $$\label{h3:geom:ordinary-root-torsor} \mathop{\mathrm{Spec}}B_0^{1/p^l}\longrightarrow\mathop{\mathrm{Spec}}B_0.$$ It is a finite flat torsor for $$\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal E[p^l],\mathcal C[p^l]),$$ a form of $\mu_{p^l}^2$. These identifications commute with the $P_3$ action, with truncation in $l$, and with Frobenius. They therefore define a natural tower of multiplicative-type torsors over the uncompleted ring $B_0$.
  - Explanation: Identifies ordinary finite-torsion splittings with the canonical root extensions, retaining multiplicative-type translations and all natural actions.
- **claim-relative-additive-presentation** (theorem, [source](#stmt-h3-ana-relative-bc)): Let $F/\mathbb Q_p$ be the unramified extension of degree $m$, embedded in $C$. There is an identification over $C^\flat$ $$N_m\simeq \mathbb G_{a,C}^{\diamond}/\underline F.$$ It is compatible with base change in $S$ and with scalar multiplication by $\mathbb Q_p^\times$. In particular $$N_m^*\simeq [(\mathbb A^1_C\setminus\underline F)^{\diamond}/\underline F].$$
  - Explanation: Presents the negative extension space as an additive-line quotient and identifies its punctured locus compatibly with scalar actions and base change.
- **claim-kummer-annulus-contraction** (bound, [source](#stmt-h3-ana-annulus-contraction)): Fix a topological generator of $\mathbb Z_p(1)$, let $\epsilon\in C^\flat$ be its compatible system of roots, and put $\theta=\|\epsilon-1\|<1$. Consider an untilted closed annulus $A[r,b]=\{r\leq \|z\|\leq b\}$ and a smaller annulus $A[r',b']$ satisfying $$r'\geq r/\theta,\qquad b'\leq\theta b.$$ In the Kummer cochain models, restriction is homotopic to its constant-monomial part. That part is $R\oplus R(-1)[-1]$. The homotopy on the nonconstant part is bounded by one in these two Gauss norms. The assertion holds uniformly after $R$ is replaced by $C_{\mathrm{cts}}(T,R)$.
  - Explanation: Contracts the nonconstant Kummer monomials across the stated radius gaps with a uniform bounded homotopy, including continuous parameters.
- **claim-analytic-limit-acyclicity** (theorem, [source](#stmt-h3-ana-analytic-limits)): Let $M_0\leftarrow M_1\leftarrow\cdots$ be a tower of complete nonarchimedean Banach spaces with dense transition maps of norm at most one. Its derived inverse limit has no higher cohomology. The assertion remains true after applying $C_{\mathrm{cts}}(T,-)$. In particular it applies to the tilted Laurent algebras on an exhaustion by closed smaller annuli or polyannuli.
  - Explanation: Eliminates higher derived inverse limits for complete Banach towers with dense contractive transitions, also after continuous profinite families.
- **claim-affine-zero-section-purity** (theorem, [source](#stmt-h3-ana-affine-purity)): For every $d\geq1$ and every $S,T$ as above, the natural maps give $$R\Gamma(\mathbb A^d_S,\mathcal O^\flat)=R, \qquad R\Gamma_{0}(\mathbb A^d_S,\mathcal O^\flat) =R(-d)[-2d].$$ The first identification is the map of constants. The second is the product of the normal Kummer classes. It is natural under translation of the section and invertible linear changes of the normal coordinates. The equalities are relative equalities, including the continuous parameters $T$.
  - Explanation: Computes relative affine constants and zero-section support through normal Kummer classes, with coordinate naturality and parameters.
- **claim-rational-family-support** (theorem, [source](#stmt-h3-ana-tube-purity)): The following supports in an untilted relative affine line have cohomology $$R\Gamma_Z(\mathbb A^1_S,\mathcal O^\flat) \simeq\mathcal D_{\mathrm{lf}}(Z,R)(-1)[-2]:$$* 1. *a constant finite extension $F\subset C$ of $\mathbb Q_p$;* 2. *the image of $(a,b)\mapsto az+b$, with $a,b\in\mathbb Q_p$ and $z$ a section of the relative affine line whose value in each geometric untilt lies outside $\mathbb Q_p$; one may also restrict $a$ to a compact open subset.* *These are relative identifications, natural for the translations and linear changes preserving the indicated support. They retain all profinite parameters. Taking products of the first support in two separate coordinates gives $$R\Gamma_{F^2}(\mathbb A^2_S,\mathcal O^\flat) \simeq\mathcal D_{\mathrm{lf}}(F^2,R)(-2)[-4].$$
  - Explanation: Computes support in the specified rational families as locally finite distributions and retains product supports, orientations, and parameters.
- **claim-translation-orientation** (theorem, [source](#stmt-h3-ana-translations)): Let $F/\mathbb Q_p$ have degree $m$, acting by translations. Then $$R\Gamma_{\mathrm{cts}}(F,R)=R,\qquad R\Gamma_{\mathrm{cts}}(F,\mathcal D_{\mathrm{lf}}(F,R)) =R\otimes_{\mathbb F_p}\operatorname{or}_F[-m].$$ Here $\operatorname{or}_F$ is the inverse orientation of the $m$-dimensional translation group. With the convention that $a$ acts on points by $z\mapsto az$, a scalar $a\in\mathbb Z_p^\times$ acts on this line by $\bar a^{-m}$. The assertions and their support maps hold with continuous profinite parameters.
  - Explanation: Computes translation cohomology of constants and distributions and identifies the inverse scalar orientation character.
- **claim-punctured-negative-cohomology** (theorem, [source](#stmt-h3-prop-punctured-cohomology)): For $m=1,2$ the natural constants map fits into a fiber sequence $$R\longrightarrow R\Gamma(N_m^*,\mathcal O^\flat) \longrightarrow R(-1)\otimes\operatorname{or}_F[-m-1].$$ It is equivariant for scalar units and natural in $S$ and in profinite parameters. Thus the only cohomology groups are $R$ in degree zero and an orientation line in degree $m+1$. The scalar $a\in\mathbb Z_p^\times$ has weight $\bar a^{-m}$ on the latter. Reversing the action convention reverses all these exponents simultaneously.
  - Explanation: Places punctured negative-space cohomology in the constants row and the stated orientation row with its full scalar action.
- **claim-ordinary-support-characters** (classification, [source](#stmt-h3-ana-ordinary-support)): The support at the double origin in $N^2$ is a line in degree six, of scalar weight $-2$. The support in $D$ has cohomology in degrees three and five. In each degree it is a distribution module on $\mathbb P^1(\mathbb Q_p)$ with a one-dimensional continuous fiber. The scalar weights of these two fibers are respectively $-1$ and $-2$.* *These descriptions are equivariant relative descriptions, with continuous profinite parameters. For the stabilizer of the direction $(1,0)$, written $$B=\left\{\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\0&d\end{pmatrix} \in\mathop{\mathrm{GL}}_2(\mathbb Z_p)\right\},$$ the two fibers have characters $\bar d^{-1}$ and $\bar a^{-1}\bar d^{-1}$. An element $v\in P_1=\mathbb Z_p^\times$ has characters $\bar v$ and $\bar v^2$, respectively. Normal Kummer twists are understood in these descriptions.
  - Explanation: Identifies the origin and dependent-pair support rows, their distribution fibers, and their stabilizer and quotient-frame characters.
- **claim-ordinary-geometric-constants** (theorem, [source](#stmt-h3-prop-ordinary-constants)): For $p\geq5$, the structure map $Y_1\to BG_f$ and the coefficient unit induce an equivalence $$R\Gamma_{\mathrm{cts}}(G_f,R) \xrightarrow{\ \simeq\ } R\Gamma(Y_1,\mathcal O^\flat).$$ This is an equivalence of derived algebras and is natural over $S$, with continuous profinite parameters. It retains both frame-group actions before taking their cohomology. In particular the degree-three class from the rank-two Tate frame is carried by this actual map from constants.
  - Explanation: Proves that the actual structure map and coefficient unit compute ordinary geometric cohomology as the frame-group derived algebra.
- **claim-induced-measure-finiteness** (theorem, [source](#stmt-h3-ana-measure-induction)): Let $G$ be a compact $p$-adic analytic group without $p$-torsion, let $B\subset G$ be a closed analytic subgroup without $p$-torsion, and suppose $G\to G/B$ has continuous local sections. If $V$ is a finite-dimensional continuous $k$-representation of $B$, then $$M=k[[G]]\widehat\otimes_{k[[B]]}V$$ has finite-dimensional continuous $G$-cohomology in every degree. The same cohomology after replacing coefficient copies of $k$ by $R$ is the corresponding finite-dimensional cohomology tensored with $R$, including continuous profinite parameters.
  - Explanation: Proves finite-dimensional cohomology for the specified induced measure modules and preserves scalar extension and profinite parameters.
- **claim-twisted-ordinary-finiteness** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-h3-ana-twisted-finiteness)): If a coefficient line on $Y_1$ becomes a finite-character constant line on $E_1$, its geometric cohomology is finite-dimensional in every degree and vanishes outside a finite range. This applies to all powers of the periodicity line and all finite tame determinant twists. For a profinite parameter $T$, the corresponding cohomology is $C_{\mathrm{cts}}(T,-)$ of this finite-dimensional answer.
  - Explanation: Extends geometric finiteness and bounded cohomological range to coefficient lines trivialized with finite characters on the independent locus.
- **claim-base-frobenius-exactness** (theorem, [source](#stmt-h3-ana-base-frobenius)): Let $q=\|k\|$, and let $M_k$ be the analytic function space over $k$ on a chosen perfected punctured ball or on the perfected ordinary polyannular open. Let $M_C$ be the corresponding function space after extension from $k$ to $C^\flat$. Let $\varphi$ act as the $q$-th power on coefficients and fix the variables. Then $$0\longrightarrow M_k\longrightarrow M_C \xrightarrow{\varphi-1}M_C\longrightarrow0$$ is exact, including after $C_{\mathrm{cts}}(T,-)$ for a profinite space $T$. The same statement applies to finite products of the punctured-ball charts at finite marking levels. Consequently the coefficient comparison is an equality with derived base-Frobenius invariants, naturally for all group actions defined over $k$.
  - Explanation: Identifies analytic coefficients over the finite field with derived base-Frobenius invariants, preserving factor permutations, group actions, and parameters.
- **claim-completed-strata-comparisons** (theorem, [source](#stmt-h3-thm-completed-cohomology)): The completed strata of [h3:thm:coordinate-comparison](#h3:thm:coordinate-comparison) have the following properties.* 1. *For the ordinary completed coefficient ring $B_{\mathrm{pk}}$, the natural constants map is an equivalence $$R\Gamma_{\mathrm{cts}}(\mathop{\mathrm{GL}}_2(\mathbb Z_p)\times P_1,k) \xrightarrow{\ \simeq\ } R\Gamma_{\mathrm{cts}}(P_3,B_{\mathrm{pk}}).$$ It is the map defined by $Y_1\to B(\mathop{\mathrm{GL}}_2(\mathbb Z_p)\times P_1)$, and is compatible with geometric constant extension, products, coefficient Frobenius, and profinite parameters. Every periodicity twist and finite tame character twist has finite cohomology in each degree, in a bounded range.* 2. *Let $L$ be the connected height-two marking algebra, $U\subset P_2$ an open subgroup, $B=L^U$, and $B^{\mathrm b}=\widehat{B^{\mathrm{perf}}}$. Finite products of fields are allowed. Then each $H^a_{\mathrm{cts}}(H,B^{\mathrm b})$ is finite-dimensional over $k$, and its degree-zero group is $k$ by constants. The same finiteness holds for lines framed on a finite connected-marking cover, including the periodicity and tame determinant lines used below. On taking the filtered colimit over marking levels there is a natural fiber sequence $$k\longrightarrow \mathop{\mathrm{colim}}_U R\Gamma_{\mathrm{cts}}(H,(L^U)^{\mathrm b}) \longrightarrow k_{\lambda}[-3].$$ The first arrow is the inclusion of constants. The full residual norm quotient $P_3/H=\mathbb Z_p^\times$ acts on $k_\lambda$ by $a\mapsto\bar a^{-2}$ in the point-action convention above. The commuting $P_2$ action is retained. It is smooth on the displayed finite-dimensional rows. The statement includes restrictions between marking levels. With a profinite parameter $T$, each displayed cohomology group is replaced by its $C_{\mathrm{cts}}(T,-)$, as specified at the start of the section.* *In particular, invariants of the order-$p-1$ subgroup of the full norm quotient kill the extra line in <span class="upright">(ii)</span>. This subgroup is in the quotient; no section of $P_3\to\mathbb Z_p^\times$ is required.
  - Explanation: Computes ordinary completed constants and finite-stage coheight-one cohomology, retaining twists, smooth frame actions, the extra norm-character row, and parameters.
- **claim-coheight-one-algebraic-constants** (theorem, [source](#stmt-h3-thm-coheight-one-comparison)): For every $p\geq5$, the natural constants map is a quasi-isomorphism $$\label{h3:co:main-constants} k\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } \mathop{\mathrm{colim}}_U C^\bullet_{\mathrm{cts}}(H',B_U).$$ It is equivariant for the commuting connected-frame action and for the remaining height-three action. For every profinite space $T$, its parameterized version $$C(T,k)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } \mathop{\mathrm{colim}}_U C\bigl(T,C^\bullet_{\mathrm{cts}}(H',B_U)\bigr)$$ is also a quasi-isomorphism. All maps are the maps induced by constants and inclusions of coefficient algebras.
  - Explanation: Computes the algebraic marking-union cochains for the full tame norm preimage by the original constants map, equivariantly and with profinite families.
- **claim-finite-continuous-resolutions** (theorem, [source](#stmt-h3-co-compact-resolution)): Let $G$ be a compact $p$-adic analytic group with no element of order $p$, and put $d=\dim G$. The trivial module $\mathbb F_p$ has a resolution of length $d$ by finitely generated projective $\mathbb F_p[[G]]$-modules. For every complete linearly topologized representation $M$ with invariant neighborhoods, applying continuous $\mathbb F_p[[G]]$-linear Hom to this resolution computes $C^\bullet_{\mathrm{cts}}(G,M)$ up to a continuous chain homotopy equivalence. Its terms are continuous direct summands of finite powers of $M$.* *If $M$ is compact, $H^a_{\mathrm{cts}}(G,M)$ is compact Hausdorff. For $G=H$ or $G=P_3$, put $d_H=8$ and $d_{P_3}=9$. Their adjoint orientation characters are trivial, and there are natural identifications $$\label{h3:co:compact-duality} H^a_{\mathrm{cts}}(G,M)^\vee \cong H^{d_G-a}_{\mathrm{cts}}(G,M^\vee), \qquad M^\vee=\mathop{\mathrm{Hom}}_{\mathrm{cts},\mathbb F_p}(M,\mathbb F_p),$$ where $M^\vee$ has its discrete topology and contragredient action. The transposed coefficient map induces the dual cohomology map. The same formula, with compact and discrete sides interchanged, holds for a discrete continuous $\mathbb F_p$-representation and its compact dual. In particular, finite coefficient modules have finite cohomology.
  - Explanation: Compares finite projective completed resolutions with continuous cochains and supplies compact/discrete duality with natural transposed coefficient maps.
- **claim-polish-strictness** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-h3-co-strictness)): Let $A^\bullet$ be a complex of Polish abelian groups with continuous differentials. If $H^a(A^\bullet)$ is finite, its quotient topology is discrete. More precisely, the boundary subgroup $B^a$ is open and closed in the cycle group $Z^a$, and $\partial:A^{a-1}\twoheadrightarrow B^a$ is open. Consequently, for every neighborhood $V$ of zero in $A^{a-1}$ there is a neighborhood $W$ of zero in $Z^a$ such that every member of $W$ has a primitive in $V$.
  - Explanation: Uses finite cohomology to make boundaries open and closed and to obtain primitives in arbitrarily prescribed neighborhoods.
- **claim-profinite-parameter-lifting** (theorem, [source](#stmt-h3-co-parameters)): Let $T$ be a profinite space.* 1. *A continuous map $T\to F$ lifts through every continuous open surjective homomorphism $E\twoheadrightarrow F$ of Polish abelian groups.* 2. *If a Polish complex $A^\bullet$ has finite cohomology in every degree, then $$H^a C(T,A^\bullet)\cong C(T,H^a(A^\bullet)),$$ where the finite cohomology group on the right is discrete.* 3. *For a filtered system of such complexes, the corresponding identity commutes with the cochain colimit, with the colimit of the cohomology groups given its discrete topology.
  - Explanation: Lifts continuous profinite families through open Polish surjections and commutes parameter cohomology with the specified filtered systems.
- **claim-distribution-parameter** (construction, [source](#stmt-h3-co-distribution)): After a finite enlargement of $k$, the inverse-limit distribution algebra of <a href="#h3:co:root-torsors" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="h3:co:root-torsors">[h3:co:root-torsors]</a> is $k[[D]]$, with a parameter $D$ having the following properties.* 1. *It acts $L$-linearly and locally nilpotently on $R$. For every $i\geq0$, $$\ker(D^{p^i}:R\to R)=L^{1/p^i}.$$ It is surjective, and $D^{p^i-1}:L^{1/p^i}\to L$ is nonzero on every factor.* 2. *It commutes with $H$. Its residual $\mu_{p-1}$-character is $\chi(u)=u^{s_{\mathrm{dist}}}$, where $s_{\mathrm{dist}}\in\{1,-1\}$. Thus $$\label{h3:co:distribution-sequence} 0\longrightarrow L\longrightarrow R \xrightarrow{D} R(\chi^{-1})\longrightarrow0$$ is an exact sequence of $H'$-modules.* 3. *If $q=p^i$, where $i$ is even and divisible by $[k:\mathbb F_p]$, then $$\label{h3:co:frobenius-distribution} D(f^q)=(D^qf)^q,\qquad D^q(z^{1/q})=(Dz)^{1/q}.$$ In particular $D^q$ is $L^{1/q}$-linear.* 4. *On any complete finite separable and root stage these operators are continuous after passage to a larger such stage. Each target stage admits a continuous additive right inverse of $D$ with values in one larger stage. Therefore <a href="#h3:co:distribution-sequence" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="h3:co:distribution-sequence">[h3:co:distribution-sequence]</a> is exact on the filtered continuous cochain complexes, with profinite parameters.
  - Explanation: Constructs the distribution parameter with its kernel filtration, residual character, Frobenius identities, continuous stage control, and cochain-exact sequence.
- **claim-cartier-distribution-traces** (theorem, [source](#stmt-h3-co-cartier-trace)): For every $i\geq1$, put $q=p^i$. There exists $c_i\in k^\times$ such that $$\label{h3:co:cartier-distribution-trace} D^{q-1}(f^{1/q})=c_i\mathcal C^i(f)\qquad(f\in L).$$ In particular, $$\label{h3:co:cartier-frobenius-zero} \mathcal C(f^p)=0.$$ At every finite separable stage $B$ containing $\eta$ there is an exact sequence of continuous $\mathbb F_p[H]$-modules $$\label{h3:co:cartier-four-term} 0\longrightarrow B\xrightarrow{\mathrm{Fr}}B \xrightarrow{d/\eta}B\xrightarrow{\mathcal C}B\longrightarrow0.$$ Here and throughout this section, $\mathrm{Fr}(f)=f^p$ is coefficient $p$-Frobenius. The ordinary-stratum argument in [h3:sec:ordinary](#h3:sec:ordinary) separately fixes a $q$-power operator. The two short exact factors of <a href="#h3:co:cartier-four-term" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="h3:co:cartier-four-term">[h3:co:cartier-four-term]</a> admit continuous additive sections onto their images. Under the residue pairing $$\label{h3:co:residue-pairing} \langle f,g\rangle_B =\sum_j\mathop{\mathrm{Tr}}_{\kappa_j/\mathbb F_p}\mathop{\mathrm{Res}}_{s_j}(fg\eta), \qquad B=\prod_j\kappa_j((s_j)),$$ the $H$-action is isometric and $\langle\mathcal C f,g\rangle_B=\langle f,g^p\rangle_B$.
  - Explanation: Relates distribution traces to the invariant Cartier operator, proves its Frobenius-zero identity, and establishes the residue transpose and continuous exact sequence.
- **claim-good-field-stages** (construction, [source](#stmt-h3-co-good-stages)): There is a cofinal family of normal open subgroups $U\subset J$ such that, for $B=B_U$, the differential $\eta$ is defined over $B$, there is $\theta\in B^{1/p}$ with $D\theta=1$, and $$\label{h3:co:good-jet} \sigma(D)-D\in D^{p+2}k[[D]]\qquad(\sigma\in U).$$ The operator $D$ restricts continuously to $B^{1/p}$. Writing $\eta=h_j(s_j)ds_j/s_j$ on each field factor, the lattice $$\label{h3:co:positive-differential-lattice} P_B=\prod_j h_j^{-1}s_j\kappa_j[[s_j]]$$ is compact, open, and preserved by $H$ and $\mathcal C$. Its annihilator for <a href="#h3:co:residue-pairing" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="h3:co:residue-pairing">[h3:co:residue-pairing]</a> is $\mathcal O_B$, and the annihilator of $\mathcal O_B$ is $P_B$.
  - Explanation: Chooses a cofinal system where the differential, distribution preimage, jet bound, and mutually annihilating stable lattices coexist.
- **claim-uncompleted-stage-finiteness** (theorem, [source](#stmt-h3-prop-finite-stage-finiteness)): Let $B=B_U$ be a good stage as in [h3:co:good-stages](#h3:co:good-stages). For every $a\geq0$, each of the following cohomology groups is finite: $$H^a_{\mathrm{cts}}(H,B),\qquad H^a_{\mathrm{cts}}(H,\Lambda),\qquad H^a_{\mathrm{cts}}(H,B/\Lambda),$$ where $\Lambda$ is any $H$-stable order lattice in $B$. The assertion holds at each finite root stage and for a coefficient line which has an $H$-invariant frame at a finite separable stage, with its order lattices and their quotients. In particular it holds for the periodicity and determinant lines used in this paper after choosing a sufficiently deep stage.
  - Explanation: Proves finite cohomology for good uncompleted fields, stable order lattices, their quotients, finite root stages, and appropriately framed coefficient lines.
- **claim-completed-positive-acyclicity** (theorem, [source](#stmt-h3-co-completed-positive)): Let $B$ be a good stage. All $H^a_{\mathrm{cts}}(H,B^b)$ are finite, and $$R\Gamma_{\mathrm{cts}}(H,(B^b)^{++})=0, \qquad (B^b)^{++}=\{f:v(f)>0\}.$$ The cohomology groups of $\mathcal O_{B^b}$ and $B^b/\mathcal O_{B^b}$ are finite as well.
  - Explanation: Makes strictly positive completed coefficients acyclic and establishes finiteness for the integral and nonintegral valuation quotients.
- **claim-finite-cartier-stable-image** (theorem, [source](#stmt-h3-co-stable-image)): For every $a$, the subgroup $$I_a=\bigcap_{n\geq0}\mathcal C^nM_a$$ is finite.
  - Explanation: Proves that the stable Cartier image in compact lattice cohomology is finite.
- **claim-compact-cartier-module** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-h3-co-compact-cartier)): Let $M$ be a compact Hausdorff $\mathbb F_p$-vector space with a continuous endomorphism $C$. Suppose that $I=\bigcap_n C^nM$ and $M/CM$ are finite. Then $C(I)=I$, the quotient $Q=M/I$ is a finitely generated $\mathbb F_p[[t]]$-module with $t$ acting as $C$, and both $Q[C^\infty]$ and $\ker(C:M\to M)$ are finite. If a $C$-stable subgroup $N\subset M$ has finite forward $C$-orbits elementwise, then $N$ is finite and $$\label{h3:co:stable-quotient} \bigcap_n\mathop{\mathrm{im}}(C^nM\longrightarrow M/N) =\mathop{\mathrm{im}}(I\longrightarrow M/N).$$
  - Explanation: Derives a finitely generated formal-power-series quotient and finite operator torsion, kernel, and finite-orbit stable subgroups from finite stable image and cokernel.
- **claim-countable-frobenius-kernel** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-h3-co-frobenius-kernel)): If $\bigcap_n\mathop{\mathrm{im}}(\mathcal C^nM_a\to X_a)$ is finite, then $\ker(\mathrm{Fr}:X_a\to X_a)$ is countable.
  - Explanation: Bounds the uncompleted Frobenius kernel by countability when the stable Cartier image in field cohomology is finite.
- **claim-positive-order-decompletion** (theorem, [source](#stmt-h3-co-decompletion)): The inclusions induce a natural quasi-isomorphism $$\label{h3:co:decompletion-map} \mathop{\mathrm{colim}}_{U,e}C^\bullet_{\mathrm{cts}}(H,B_U^{1/p^e}) \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } \mathop{\mathrm{colim}}_U C^\bullet_{\mathrm{cts}}(H,B_U^b).$$ It retains the commuting actions and remains a quasi-isomorphism after forming continuous families parametrized by any profinite space.
  - Explanation: Compares algebraic root-stage and completed perfected cochains through the natural inclusions while retaining commuting actions and profinite families.
- **claim-full-norm-weight-vanishing** (theorem, [source](#stmt-h3-lem-full-norm-weights)): On $H^*_{\mathrm{cts}}(H,R)$ the full residual norm quotient has the two characters in <a href="#h3:co:completed-input" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="h3:co:completed-input">[h3:co:completed-input]</a>. The distribution target $R(\chi^{-1})$ has no $H'$-cohomology, whereas $R\Gamma_{\mathrm{cts}}(H',R)$ is $k$ by its constants map. These assertions hold for every $p\geq5$, without choosing a subgroup section of $H'\to\mu_{p-1}$.
  - Explanation: Uses the full residual norm characters to kill the twisted distribution target and retain precisely constants in the untwisted source without a subgroup section.
- **claim-continuous-field-descent** (theorem, [source](#stmt-h3-co-field-descent)): For every profinite space $T$, the natural augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism $$\label{h3:co:field-descent-map} C(T,K)\longrightarrow \mathop{\mathrm{colim}}_U C^\bullet_{\mathrm{cts}}\bigl(J,C(T,B_U)\bigr).$$ The same statement holds for a coefficient line pulled back from $K$. These comparisons are natural in $T$ and equivariant for the commuting $P_3$-action.
  - Explanation: Descends the connected-marking field union to the base field and pulled-back lines through natural equivariant augmentations with profinite parameters.
- **claim-base-order-lattice-finiteness** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-h3-co-base-lattices)): Let $\mathcal L$ be a coefficient line over $K$ whose pullback to $L$ has an $H$-invariant frame at a finite stage. Suppose that $\Lambda\subset\mathcal L$ is a $P_3$-stable order lattice over $k[[y]]$. Then $$H^a_{\mathrm{cts}}(P_3,\Lambda) \quad\text{and}\quad H^a_{\mathrm{cts}}(H,\Lambda)$$ are finite for every $a$. This applies to every periodicity power, every finite determinant character, their inverses, and their products with conormal or canonical-line twists. In particular each adjacent $x$-pole strip used in [h3:sec:ordinary](#h3:sec:ordinary) has finite $P_3$-cohomology.
  - Explanation: Proves base-lattice cohomology finiteness for both stabilizer and norm kernel, including the twists needed for adjacent ordinary pole strips.
- **claim-exact-amitsur-error-control** (theorem, [source](#stmt-h3-lem-exact-amitsur)): Let $\mathcal C$ be a stable symmetric monoidal $\infty$-category with limits and with tensor product exact in each variable. Let $E$ be a descendable commutative algebra, write $\mathbf1$ for the unit, and put $I_E=\mathop{\mathrm{fib}}(\mathbf1\to E)$. For its full Amitsur object $C^q=E^{\otimes(q+1)}$, the partial totalization $$\operatorname{Tot}_s C^\bullet =\lim_{[q]\in\Delta_{\leq s}}C^q$$ is a finite cubical limit. Its augmentation fiber, including its map to the unit, is $$\label{h3:des:partial-amitsur-fiber} \bigl(\mathop{\mathrm{fib}}(\mathbf1\longrightarrow\operatorname{Tot}_s C^\bullet) \longrightarrow\mathbf1\bigr) \simeq \bigl(I_E^{\otimes(s+1)}\longrightarrow\mathbf1\bigr).$$ The transition between successive fibers applies $I_E\to\mathbf1$ to the last factor. There is an integer $N$ such that every composite of $N$ successive maps between these augmentation fibers is null. Every exact functor from $\mathcal C$ to a stable category preserves the augmented totalization $\mathbf1\simeq\operatorname{Tot}C^\bullet$ and this same null-composite bound.
  - Explanation: Models full partial Amitsur totalizations by finite cubes and proves a uniform null-composite bound preserved by every exact functor.
- **claim-relative-morava-descent** (theorem, [source](#stmt-h3-prop-exact-descent)): Let $n\geq1$, let $k$ be a finite field containing $F=\mathbb F_{p^n}$, and let $R_{n,k}=L_{K(n)}S_k$. In the $K(n)$-local category of $S_k$-modules, the algebra $E_n(k)$ is descendable over the unit $R_{n,k}$. Write $\widehat\otimes$ for the tensor product in this local category and put $$\mathcal N_n^q=E_n(k)^{\widehat\otimes_{R_{n,k}}(q+1)} \qquad(q\geq0).$$ Its augmented Amitsur object totalizes to $R_{n,k}$. Every exact functor from this local category to a stable category preserves that totalization and a uniform nilpotence bound for its error tower. In particular this applies to the inclusion in spectra followed by ordinary smash, a finite Moore quotient, a chromatic localization, or a monochromatic fiber.* *There are identifications of graded rings $$\label{h3:des:relative-cooperations} \pi_*\mathcal N_n^q \cong C_{\mathrm{cts}}(P_n^q,E_n(k)_*),$$ with the maximal-ideal topology on the coefficients. Under these identifications the actual cofaces and codegeneracies induce those of the continuous action cobar construction, and the augmented unit is the constant unit. Each $\mathcal N_n^q$ is an ordinary $E_n(k)$-module through its first factor. This is the module structure used when an ordinary exact functor is applied to a term.
  - Explanation: Proves relative descendability and exact-test preservation of totalization, then identifies actual relative cooperation maps with the ordinary stabilizer action cobar.
- **claim-flat-continuous-functions** (theorem, [source](#stmt-h3-des-flat-functions)): Put $\widetilde A=W(k)[[x,y]]$, and let $Q$ be profinite. The module $C_{\mathrm{cts}}(Q,\widetilde A)$, for the $(p,x,y)$-adic topology, is pro-free and flat over $\widetilde A$. For every ordinary $E_3(k)$-module $N_Q$ whose graded coefficient module is $C_{\mathrm{cts}}(Q,(E_3(k))_*)$, ordinary smash with $E_2(k)$ over the $p$-local sphere $\mathbb S_{(p)}$ has homotopy $$\label{h3:des:ordinary-kunneth} (E_2(k))_*E_3(k)\otimes_{(E_3(k))_*} C_{\mathrm{cts}}(Q,(E_3(k))_*).$$ The first tensor factor in <a href="#h3:des:ordinary-kunneth" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="h3:des:ordinary-kunneth">[h3:des:ordinary-kunneth]</a> denotes absolute ordinary cooperations over $\mathbb S_{(p)}$. This applies in particular to the actual term $N_Q=\mathcal N_3^q$ for $Q=P_3^q$, with its first-factor module structure.
  - Explanation: Proves pro-freeness and ordinary flatness of continuous coefficient functions and gives the ordinary smash-product coefficient formula for the stated module terms.
- **claim-relative-residue-cooperations** (theorem, [source](#stmt-h3-des-residue-cooperations)): Let $$\overline E_2=E_2(k)/(p,u_1).$$ Apply the ordinary relative tensor $\overline E_2\otimes_{S_k}(-)$ to the $K(3)$-completed Amitsur object for $E_3(k)$. Its homotopy is even periodic. After using the test periodicity generator, the degree-zero coefficient in cosimplicial degree $q$ is $$\mathop{\mathrm{colim}}_B C_{\mathrm{cts}}(P_3^q,B),$$ where $B$ runs through the finite connected-marking algebras over $k((y))$ of [h3:sec:coheight-one](#h3:sec:coheight-one). The cofaces give their actual $P_3$-action, and the test of the unit is the constant cochain.
  - Explanation: Identifies the ordinary relative residue test with even-periodic algebraic marking-union cochains, including actual action cofaces and the unit.
- **claim-actual-height-two-basis** (theorem, [source](#stmt-h3-thm-height-two-test)): Set $$W=L_2S\vee\Sigma^{-1}L_2S,\qquad w=(1,\zeta):W\longrightarrow X.$$ The first component is the canonical unit, and $L_{K(2)}w$ is an equivalence. More explicitly, the specified maps give $$(1,\zeta):R_2\vee\Sigma^{-1}R_2 \xrightarrow{\ \simeq\ }L_{K(2)}T.$$
  - Explanation: Proves that the same canonical unit and integral determinant maps form the height-two localized basis.
- **claim-equivariant-root-retractions** (construction, [source](#stmt-h3-ord-root-retractions)): There is a continuous $G$-equivariant $B_0$-linear retraction $B_0^{1/p}\to B_0$. Its iterates give compatible retractions from every finite root level and extend to a continuous retraction $$\rho:B_{\mathrm{pk}}\longrightarrow B_{\mathrm{hol}}$$ of the natural inclusion. For every line $\mathcal L$ above, the same construction gives a continuous equivariant retraction from $B_{\mathrm{pk}}(\mathcal L)$ to $B_{\mathrm{hol}}(\mathcal L)$. There are also an integer $e>0$, $q=p^e$, and continuous $G$-equivariant additive operators $\mathrm{Fr}$ and $\mathcal P$ on its holomorphic coefficients such that $$\label{h3:ord:retraction-identity} \mathcal P\mathrm{Fr}=1.$$ Here $\mathrm{Fr}$ is the $q$-power map in a horizontal frame. It is invertible on the perfected coefficients, preserves some $A_{-r}(\mathcal L)$, and $\mathcal P$ preserves $A_D(\mathcal L)$ for every sufficiently large $D$. All these maps are compatible with constant-field descent.
  - Explanation: Constructs compatible equivariant root projections and a holomorphic retraction, including twisted horizontal Frobenius and its left inverse.
- **claim-uniform-root-loss-bounds** (bound, [source](#stmt-h3-ord-loss-bounds)): Fix the operators of [h3:ord:root-retractions](#h3:ord:root-retractions) and a free rational frame of $\mathcal L$, using the normalized Gauss valuations just specified. There are constants $c\geq0$ and $c_{a,b}\geq0$ such that $$\begin{aligned} \mathcal P(A_L(\mathcal L)) &\subseteq A_{L/q+c}(\mathcal L),\label{h3:ord:one-pole-bound}\\ v_{a,b}(\mathcal Pf) &\geq q^{-1}v_{a,b}(f)-c_{a,b}. \label{h3:ord:one-norm-bound} \end{aligned}$$ For real indices the pole inequality defines the lattice, so $A_t=A_{\lfloor t\rfloor}$ in the original integral frame. With $C=c/(1-q^{-1})$ and $C_{a,b}=c_{a,b}/(1-q^{-1})$, iteration gives $$\begin{aligned} \mathcal P^n(A_L(\mathcal L)) &\subseteq A_{q^{-n}L+C}(\mathcal L),\label{h3:ord:iterated-poles}\\ v_{a,b}(\mathcal P^nf) &\geq q^{-n}v_{a,b}(f)-C_{a,b}. \label{h3:ord:iterated-norms} \end{aligned}$$ The losses for $\rho_n$ in <a href="#h3:ord:finite-root-projection" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="h3:ord:finite-root-projection">[h3:ord:finite-root-projection]</a> are therefore independent of the root level.
  - Explanation: Bounds pole and Gauss-valuation losses under the root projection and its iterates uniformly over root levels.
- **claim-holomorphic-perfect-comparison** (theorem, [source](#stmt-h3-prop-holomorphic-comparison)): For every specified coefficient line the natural map $$R\Gamma_{\mathrm{cts}}(G,B_{\mathrm{hol}}(\mathcal L)) \longrightarrow R\Gamma_{\mathrm{cts}}(G,B_{\mathrm{pk}}(\mathcal L))$$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Its cohomology groups are finite, and the chosen Frobenius power acts invertibly on them. For a profinite parameter space $T$, the comparison and Frobenius invertibility persist, and the cohomology is naturally $$C\bigl(T,H^a_{\mathrm{cts}}(G,B_{\mathrm{hol}}(\mathcal L))\bigr),$$ where the finite point-value cohomology group has its discrete topology. Finiteness is asserted for the cohomology without parameters. The comparison is compatible with coefficient-field descent. For the untwisted line it identifies the natural constants comparison of [h3:prop:ordinary-constants](#h3:prop:ordinary-constants).
  - Explanation: Compares holomorphic and perfected cohomology with finite point-valued groups and invertible chosen Frobenius, preserving parameters and constants.
- **claim-compact-laurent-tail-contraction** (bound, [source](#stmt-h3-ord-tail-contraction)): Choose an integer $D>C$ in [h3:ord:loss-bounds](#h3:ord:loss-bounds). For every compact subset $K\subset B_{\mathrm{hol}}(\mathcal L)$, $$T_D\mathcal P^nf\longrightarrow0 \quad\hbox{uniformly for }f\in K$$ in every defining Gauss norm.
  - Explanation: Proves uniform convergence of iterated Laurent tails on compact holomorphic families in every defining Gauss norm.
- **claim-ordinary-compact-stable-image** (theorem, [source](#stmt-h3-ord-stable-image)): For $D$ as above and every $a\geq0$, put $$M=H^a_{\mathrm{cts}}(G,A_D(\mathcal L)),\qquad \phi:M\longrightarrow H^a_{\mathrm{cts}}(G,B_{\mathrm{hol}}(\mathcal L)).$$ Then $M$ is compact Hausdorff, and $\mathcal P^nz\to0$ for every $z\in\ker\phi$. Moreover its stable image $$M_\infty=\bigcap_{n\geq0}\mathcal P^nM$$ is finite.
  - Explanation: Makes lattice cohomology compact Hausdorff, contracts the comparison kernel, and proves finiteness of its stable root-projection image.
- **claim-all-ordinary-lattices-finite** (theorem, [source](#stmt-h3-prop-ordinary-lattice-finiteness)): For every $a\geq0$, $d\in\mathbb Z$, and coefficient line $\mathcal L$ specified above, the group $$H^a_{\mathrm{cts}}(P_3,A_d(\mathcal L))$$ is finite. This includes all periodicity, determinant, conormal, and canonical-line twists and their inverses, with the original $(x,y)$-adic lattice topology. The conclusion uses no finiteness or cohomology comparison for $B_0$.
  - Explanation: Proves finite cohomology for all specified ordinary compact pole lattices and twists before invoking bounded-pole comparison.
- **claim-intermediate-homotopy-finiteness** (theorem, [source](#stmt-h3-des-monochromatic-finiteness)): The groups $$\pi_j(T/p),\qquad \pi_j(M_3S/p),\qquad \pi_j(X/p),\qquad \pi_j(L_1X/p)$$ are finite for every integer $j$. This assertion uses [h3:prop:ordinary-lattice-finiteness](#h3:prop:ordinary-lattice-finiteness) but does not use [h3:thm:ordinary-comparison](#h3:thm:ordinary-comparison).
  - Explanation: Proves degreewise finite Moore-quotient homotopy for the local sphere, monochromatic fiber, overlap, and its height-one localization independently of ordinary comparison.
- **claim-bounded-pole-cohomology-finite** (theorem, [source](#stmt-h3-prop-bounded-pole-finiteness)): For every $a\geq0$, the group $H^a_{\mathrm{cts}}(P_3,B_0)$, with the prescribed bounded-pole cochain convention, is finite.
  - Explanation: Proves finite algebraic ordinary cohomology under the prescribed common bounded-pole convention.
- **claim-natural-ordinary-comparison** (theorem, [source](#stmt-h3-thm-ordinary-comparison)): The natural coefficient maps induce quasi-isomorphisms $$\label{h3:ord:natural-comparison} \mathop{\mathrm{colim}}_d C^\bullet_{\mathrm{cts}}(P_3,x^{-d}A) \longrightarrow C^\bullet_{\mathrm{cts}}(P_3,B_{\mathrm{hol}}) \longrightarrow C^\bullet_{\mathrm{cts}}(P_3,B_{\mathrm{pk}}).$$ They preserve products, constants, and coefficient-field descent, and remain quasi-isomorphisms with any profinite space of continuous parameters in the convention <a href="#h3:ord:cochain-colimit" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="h3:ord:cochain-colimit">[h3:ord:cochain-colimit]</a>. Every Frobenius power, including the $p$th-power map, acts invertibly on these untwisted cohomology groups. Consequently there is the natural identification $$H^*_{\mathrm{cts}}(P_3,B_0) \cong H^*_{\mathrm{cts}}(P_1\times\mathop{\mathrm{GL}}_2(\mathbb Z_p),k).$$
  - Explanation: Identifies bounded-pole, holomorphic, and perfected cohomology through natural inclusions and computes their endpoint by frame-group constants.
- **claim-ordinary-exterior-generators** (classification, [source](#stmt-h3-ord-exterior-classes)): For $p\geq5$ the last group in [h3:thm:ordinary-comparison](#h3:thm:ordinary-comparison) is $$\Lambda_k(h,e,d),\qquad \|h\|=\|e\|=1,\quad \|d\|=3.$$ Here $h$ is the logarithmic class of $P_1=\mathbb Z_p^\times$, $e$ is the determinant logarithm of $\mathop{\mathrm{GL}}_2(\mathbb Z_p)$, and $d$ restricts to the orientation class of $\mathop{\mathrm{SL}}_2(\mathbb Z_p)$. All three classes have integral lifts in continuous $\mathbb Z_p$-cohomology of these frame groups.
  - Explanation: Computes ordinary frame cohomology as the stated exterior algebra with connected logarithm, determinant logarithm, orientation, and integral lifts.
- **claim-compatible-finite-frame-cohomology** (classification, [source](#stmt-h3-des-frame-cohomology)): For every $\ell\geq1$, there are compatible choices of generators for which $$H^*_{\mathrm{cts}}(G_{\mathrm f},\mathbb Z/p^\ell) =\Lambda_{\mathbb Z/p^\ell}(h,e,d), \qquad \|h\|=\|e\|=1,\quad \|d\|=3.$$ The degree-one generators are the two normalized logarithms, and the restriction of $d$ to $\mathop{\mathrm{SL}}_2(\mathbb Z_p)$ is its orientation generator. Coefficient extension to $W_\ell(k)$ gives the same exterior algebra over $W_\ell(k)$. These generators are fixed by the changes of integral frames and by coefficient Frobenius.
  - Explanation: Computes compatible exterior generators at every finite coefficient length and preserves frame transport, Witt scalar extension, and coefficient Frobenius.
- **claim-actual-unit-logarithm-directions** (theorem, [source](#stmt-h3-des-unit-directions)): Under the natural ordinary coefficient comparison, the map from the height-one sphere sends its degree-minus-one mod-$p$ generator to the connected logarithm $h$. Under the same comparison, the mod-$p$ reduction of the normalized height-three logarithm detecting $\zeta$ has image $$a h+b e,\qquad a,b\in\mathbb F_p,\quad b\ne0.$$ Thus, writing $\zeta$ also for its image, the ordinary mod-$p$ coefficient algebra is $$\mathbb F_p[v_1^{\pm1}]\otimes\Lambda_{\mathbb F_p}(h,\zeta,d).$$ In this formula the degree-minus-one $h$-action is the action of the actual unit $R_1\to L_{K(1)}T$.
  - Explanation: Identifies the actual height-one unit direction and shows that the height-three determinant logarithm supplies an independent exterior direction.
- **claim-last-ghost-comparison** (construction, [source](#stmt-h3-lem-ghost-comparison)): For each $\ell\geq1$, the last-ghost formula $$\label{h3:des:ghost-formula} \gamma_\ell(a_0,\ldots,a_{\ell-1}) =\sum_{i=0}^{\ell-1} p^i\widetilde a_i^{\,p^{\ell-1-i}}\quad\hbox{in }D_\ell$$ for arbitrary lifts $\widetilde a_i\in D_\ell$ defines a natural equivariant unital ring map $$W_\ell(B_0)\xrightarrow{\gamma_\ell}D_\ell.$$ Both this map and the natural coefficient map $$\beta_\ell:W_\ell(B_0)\longrightarrow W_\ell(B_{\mathrm{pk}})$$ induce isomorphisms on $P_3$-cohomology with the prescribed cochain conventions. For $\ell\geq2$, let $R_\ell:W_\ell(B_0)\to W_{\ell-1}(B_0)$ be Witt truncation and let $\operatorname{red}_{\ell,\ell-1}:D_\ell\to D_{\ell-1}$ be coefficient reduction. Then $$\label{h3:des:ghost-transition} \operatorname{red}_{\ell,\ell-1}\gamma_\ell =\gamma_{\ell-1}R_\ell W_\ell(\phi_p) \qquad(\ell\geq2).$$ The map $\gamma_\ell$ fixes the constant $\mathbb Z/p^\ell=W_\ell(\mathbb F_p)$.
  - Explanation: Constructs the natural last-ghost map, proves both finite Witt comparisons on cohomology, and records the Frobenius-twisted reduction relation and fixed prime-field constants.
- **claim-finite-witt-constants** (theorem, [source](#stmt-h3-des-witt-constants)): The actual ordinary constants map gives natural equivalences $$\eta_\ell: R\Gamma_{\mathrm{cts}}(G_{\mathrm f},W_\ell(k)) \xrightarrow{\ \simeq\ } R\Gamma_{\mathrm{cts}}(P_3,W_\ell(B_{\mathrm{pk}})).$$ They commute with truncation, coefficient Frobenius, and the maps from $\mathbb Z/p^\ell$ constants. The maps $\beta_\ell,\gamma_\ell$ in [h3:lem:ghost-comparison](#h3:lem:ghost-comparison) preserve these latter constant maps as well.
  - Explanation: Carries the actual constants equivalence through finite Witt lengths with truncation, Frobenius, and prime-field coefficient maps intact.
- **claim-finite-length-ordinary-descent** (theorem, [source](#stmt-h3-des-finite-length-model)): The ordinary spectrum $L_1(T/p^\ell)$ is the totalization of the termwise $L_1(-/p^\ell)$ Morava descent object. Its terms are even, and their internal degree-zero cochain complex is the $D_\ell$ complex above. The corresponding spectral sequence is strongly convergent, has columns $0\leq s\leq5$, and has no differentials. All its abutment groups are finite in each stem. In particular there is a natural identification $$\label{h3:des:minus-three-edge} \pi_{-3}L_1(T/p^\ell) \cong H^3_{\mathrm{cts}}(G_3(k),D_\ell),$$ where the right side includes the coefficient Galois descent just described.
  - Explanation: Identifies the finite-length ordinary descent object, its collapsed bounded spectral sequence, finite abutments, and natural degree-minus-three edge.
- **claim-height-one-derived-completion** (theorem, [source](#stmt-h3-lem-height-one-completion)): Let $M$ be an $E(1)$-local $S$-module. The natural map $$M\longrightarrow \widehat M_p:= \operatorname*{holim}_{\ell\geq1} M/p^\ell$$ is its $K(1)$-localization in $S$-modules. Here $M/p^\ell$ is the cofiber of multiplication by $p^\ell$, with the ordinary Moore quotient transitions.
  - Explanation: Identifies the natural derived Moore-quotient completion of an already height-one local module with its height-one Morava localization.
- **claim-integral-orientation-generator** (construction, [source](#stmt-h3-prop-integral-delta)): There is a class $$\delta\in\pi_{-3}L_{K(1)}T$$ whose reduction is the orientation generator $d$ in [h3:des:unit-directions](#h3:des:unit-directions). Moreover, $$\pi_{-3}L_{K(1)}T\cong\mathbb Z_p,$$ with $\delta$ a generator after the chosen orientation normalization. The finite-length identifications used to construct it preserve the given maps from $P_3$-cochains with integral constant coefficients.
  - Explanation: Constructs the integral orientation generator by compatible finite-length classes and preserves the specified maps from integral constants.
- **claim-actual-height-one-basis** (theorem, [source](#stmt-h3-thm-height-one-maps)): The integral classes $\zeta$ and $\delta$ above and the canonical unit define an equivalence $$(1,\zeta,\delta,\zeta\delta): R_1\vee\Sigma^{-1}R_1\vee \Sigma^{-3}R_1\vee\Sigma^{-4}R_1 \xrightarrow{\ \simeq\ }L_{K(1)}T.$$ The maps use the $R_1$-action and the multiplication induced from $T$. In particular the first two components are the $K(1)$-localizations of the same maps from $S$ used in [h3:thm:height-two-test](#h3:thm:height-two-test).
  - Explanation: Proves the actual localized equivalence from the unit, determinant, integral orientation, and their product while retaining the same initial sphere maps.
- **claim-natural-finite-classifying-maps** (construction, [source](#stmt-h3-rat-finite-classifying)): For a $G$-space $X$ over $B$ there is a natural finite coefficient map $$\label{h3:eq:rat-finite-classifying} \mathsf u_{X,G,\ell}: C^\bullet_{\mathrm{cts}}(G,\Lambda_\ell) \longrightarrow \operatorname{Tot}_{[a]\in\Delta} R\Gamma_v(X\times\underline{G^a},\Lambda_\ell) \simeq R\Gamma_v([X/G],\Lambda_\ell).$$ For a $G$-torsor $T\to Z$ over $B$ with relative classifying map $c_T:Z\to\mathrm B_B G$, this gives $$\operatorname{cl}_{c_T,\ell} :=c_T^*\mathsf u_{B,G,\ell}: C^\bullet_{\mathrm{cts}}(G,\Lambda_\ell) \longrightarrow R\Gamma_v(Z,\Lambda_\ell).$$ It equals <a href="#h3:eq:rat-finite-classifying" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="h3:eq:rat-finite-classifying">[h3:eq:rat-finite-classifying]</a> for $X=T$ under $[T/G]\simeq Z$. These maps commute with continuous group homomorphisms and extension of torsor structure, equivariant maps, base change, base automorphisms with compatible descent, coefficient reductions, and cup products. They also commute with the finite coefficient units $\Lambda_\ell=W_\ell(\mathbb F_p)\to W_\ell\mathcal O^\flat$. Their derived coefficient limits and their rationalizations define maps denoted $\operatorname{cl}_{c_T,\mathrm{int}}$ and $\operatorname{cl}_{c_T,\mathrm b}$ on the corresponding cohomology.* *For an algebraically closed perfectoid field $C$ of characteristic zero, put $B_C=\operatorname{Spa}(C,\mathcal O_C)^\diamond$. For every profinite $Q$ and every finite constant coefficient module $A$ on $B_C$, the actual constants map is an equivalence $$\label{h3:eq:rat-geometric-point-constants} C_{\mathrm{cts}}(Q,A)[0] \xrightarrow{\ \simeq\ } R\Gamma_v(B_C\times\underline Q,A).$$ This is natural in $Q$, in $A$, and in base automorphisms with their actions on $A$. In particular it includes the finite Tate fibers $\Lambda_\ell(-j)$. For compact $G$, it makes $\mathsf u_{B_C,G,\ell}$ an equivalence.
  - Explanation: Constructs finite-coefficient classifying maps with torsor, arithmetic, product, Witt-unit, and base-change naturality, and proves the geometric-point constants comparison.
- **claim-rational-trace-groups** (theorem, [source](#stmt-h3-rat-trace-groups)): The groups $P_3$, $J_3$, and $\mathop{\mathrm{GL}}_2(\mathbb Z_p)$ have rational cohomology $H^1_{\mathrm b}=\mathbb Q_p$, $H^2_{\mathrm b}=0$, and $H^3_{\mathrm b}=\mathbb Q_p$. They admit nonzero classes $e_3$, $e_J$, and $e_2$, respectively, whose rational Lie-algebra images are nonzero multiples of the displayed trace form. For every compact open $K\subset J_3$, restriction followed by the compact Lie-algebra comparison identifies $H^*_{\mathrm b}(J_3)$ with $H^*(\mathfrak{gl}_3,\mathbb Q_p)$; the identifications for different $K$ agree under further restriction. For $$D=\left\{\begin{pmatrix}A&v\\0&a\end{pmatrix}: A\in\mathop{\mathrm{GL}}_2(\mathbb Z_p),\ a\in\mathbb Z_p^\times,\ v\in\mathbb Q_p^2\right\},$$ write $\iota:D\to J_3$ and $\rho:D\to\mathop{\mathrm{GL}}_2(\mathbb Z_p)$ for inclusion and projection. Then $$\label{h3:eq:rat-parabolic-trace} \iota^*e_J=b\rho^*e_2\quad\text{for some }b\in\mathbb Q_p^\times.$$
  - Explanation: Computes the stated low-degree rational group cohomology, constructs nonzero trace classes, and identifies the parabolic restriction with the rank-two trace.
- **claim-modification-stack-presentations** (construction, [source](#stmt-h3-rat-modification-presentations)): Let $\mathcal M$ classify a form of $V_3$ with $P_3$-structure and a quotient line at $\infty$. There are equivalences $$\label{h3:eq:rat-two-presentations} \mathcal M\simeq[\mathbf P^2_C/P_3] \simeq[\Omega_C^2/J_3].$$ The relative classifying maps $$c_{3,\mathcal M}:\mathcal M\longrightarrow\mathrm B_{B_C}P_3, \qquad c_{J,\mathcal M}:\mathcal M\longrightarrow\mathrm B_{B_C}J_3$$ record the positive bundle and its lower modification, respectively. For the prescribed finite unramified field $F=W(k)[1/p]$, these presentations carry a common semilinear arithmetic action of $G_F$ over its action on $B_C$, commuting with both constant groups and inducing the usual action on $\Omega_C^2$.
  - Explanation: Identifies the modification stack through its positive-bundle and lower-modification frames with a common semilinear arithmetic action.
- **claim-projective-rational-splitting** (theorem, [source](#stmt-h3-rat-fixed-projective)): The first presentation in <a href="#h3:eq:rat-two-presentations" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="h3:eq:rat-two-presentations">[h3:eq:rat-two-presentations]</a> has a natural arithmetic-equivariant splitting $$\label{h3:eq:rat-projective-h3} H^3_{\mathrm b}(\mathcal M) =H^3_{\mathrm b}(P_3)\oplus H^1_{\mathrm b}(P_3)(-1),$$ whose first inclusion is the classifying map $\operatorname{cl}_{c_{3,\mathcal M},\mathrm b}$ of [h3:rat:finite-classifying](#h3:rat:finite-classifying).
  - Explanation: Splits rational degree-three modification cohomology arithmetically and identifies the first summand with the specified classifying map.
- **claim-solid-finite-resolution-descent** (theorem, [source](#stmt-h3-rat-solid-resolution)): The complexes $\mathscr C_Z$ are bounded below, derived solid, and derived $p$-complete. Let $G$ be a compact $p$-adic analytic group without $p$-torsion. There is a finite projective resolution $P_\bullet\to\mathbb Z_p$ over $\Lambda_G=\mathbb Z_p[[G]]$, with finitely generated terms and length $\dim G$, such that, for every derived solid $\underline{\mathbb Z_p}$-module complex $K$ with $\underline{\mathbb Z_p}$-linear continuous $G$-action, $$\label{h3:eq:rat-solid-hom} R\Gamma(G,K)(*)\simeq\mathop{\mathrm{Hom}}_{\Lambda_G}(P_\bullet,K).$$ Here $\mathop{\mathrm{Hom}}$ is the external complex of morphisms in solid $\underline{\Lambda_G}$-modules. A continuous action means an actual module over $\underline{\mathbb Z_p}[\underline G]$ in the derived condensed category, rather than an action on $K(*)$. If $K$ is bounded below, and an operator $\gamma$ commuting with $G$ acts by the scalar $\lambda_j\in\mathbb Q_p$ on $H^j(K)(*)[1/p]$, it acts by $\lambda_j$ on $H^s(G,H^j(K))(*)[1/p]$ for every $s$. For $K=\mathscr C_Z$ the resulting spectral sequence is $$\label{h3:eq:rat-solid-descent} H^s(G,H^j(\mathscr C_Z))(*)[1/p] \ \Longrightarrow\ H^{s+j}_{\mathrm b}([Z/G]),$$ with a finite filtration in each total degree.
  - Explanation: Computes geometric derived invariants by finite projective solid resolutions, justifying point-valued scalar actions and finite-filtration descent.
- **claim-proportional-modification-traces** (theorem, [source](#stmt-h3-rat-two-traces)): On $\mathcal M$, abbreviate the classifying images $\operatorname{cl}_{c_{3,\mathcal M},\mathrm b}(e_3)$ and $\operatorname{cl}_{c_{J,\mathcal M},\mathrm b}(e_J)$ by $e_3$ and $e_J$. Both are nonzero and satisfy $e_3=\kappa e_J$ for some $\kappa\in\mathbb Q_p^\times$. We retain this abbreviation for subsequent pullbacks from $\mathcal M$.
  - Explanation: Proves that both actual classifying trace images on the modification stack are nonzero and span the same rational line.
- **claim-ordinary-kernel-trace-transport** (theorem, [source](#stmt-h3-prop-trace-transport)): There is $a\in\mathbb Q_p^\times$ such that $$\label{h3:eq:rat-ordinary-traces} e_3=a e_2\quad\text{in }H^3_{\mathrm b}(\mathcal Y_{1,C}).$$ The class $e_2$ is pulled back from the actual integral frame group of the rank-two kernel.
  - Explanation: Transports the height-three trace to the actual integral rank-two kernel frame through adapted modification torsors.
- **claim-witt-deformation-nonvanishing** (theorem, [source](#stmt-h3-rat-witt-nonvanishing)): The right vertical map of <a href="#h3:eq:rat-witt-square" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="h3:eq:rat-witt-square">[h3:eq:rat-witt-square]</a> is injective after inversion of $p$. The Witt coefficient image of $e_3$ on $\mathcal Y_1$ is nonzero. Its corresponding image under the actual ordinary deformation-coefficient map is nonzero.
  - Explanation: Proves rational injectivity under Witt base change and follows the nonzero constant trace through the actual ordinary deformation-coefficient maps.
- **claim-rational-primitive-constant-origin** (construction, [source](#stmt-h3-lem-constants-origin)): The reduced-trace class in $H^3_{\mathrm b}(P_3)$, after the constant coefficient map and coefficient-field descent, is the degree-three class of an element $\alpha_3\in\pi_{-3}L_0T$. This element is nonzero and its image in $\pi_{-3}L_0L_{K(1)}T$ is nonzero.
  - Explanation: Realizes the descended constant trace as an actual nonzero rational sphere class whose actual height-one localization remains nonzero.
- **claim-product-compatible-rational-basis** (theorem, [source](#stmt-h3-thm-rational-compatibility)): The generators in <a href="#h3:eq:framework-rational-boundary" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="h3:eq:framework-rational-boundary">[h3:eq:framework-rational-boundary]</a> may be chosen so that $\alpha_1=\zeta$ and the actual localization map $T\to L_{K(1)}T$ satisfies $$\label{h3:eq:rat-actual-images} \alpha_3\longmapsto c\delta,\qquad \zeta\alpha_3\longmapsto c\zeta\delta \qquad(c\in\mathbb Q_p^\times)$$ after rationalization. In particular the rational homotopy of $T$ has basis $$1,\ \zeta,\ \alpha_3,\ \zeta\alpha_3,\ \alpha_5,\ \zeta\alpha_5,\ \alpha_3\alpha_5,\ \zeta\alpha_3\alpha_5$$ in degrees $0,-1,-3,-4,-5,-6,-8,-9$, respectively.
  - Explanation: Chooses rational exterior generators compatible with the actual determinant and orientation maps, with the same nonzero scalar on their product.
- **claim-canonical-map-attachment-test** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-prop-attachment-criterion)): If $u_X$ does not kill $\beta_3\in\pi_{-3}L_0X$, then $$d_3:U_3=\Sigma^{-3}L_1S\longrightarrow\Sigma W$$ is nonzero as a map of underlying spectra.
  - Explanation: Shows that survival of the chosen rational primitive under the canonical height-two localization prevents the first middle attachment from being null as a spectral map.
- **claim-nonzero-first-middle-attachment** (theorem, [source](#stmt-cor-nonzero-attachment)): For every prime $p\geq5$, retain the common height-three choice in [sec:application](#sec:application), which realizes [thm:main](#thm:main) and the height-three instance of [thm:attachment-identification](#thm:attachment-identification). Then $$d_3:\Sigma^{-3}L_1S\longrightarrow \Sigma\bigl(L_2S\vee\Sigma^{-1}L_2S\bigr)$$ is nonzero as a map of underlying spectra.
  - Explanation: Uses the companion canonical-map result to prove nonvanishing of the first height-one attachment for the common filtration choices.
- **claim-rational-height-three-algebra** (classification, [source](#stmt-h3-prop-rational-boundary)): For every prime $p\geq5$, there is an isomorphism of graded algebras $$\pi_*L_0T\simeq\Lambda_{\mathbb Q_p}(\alpha_1,\alpha_3,\alpha_5), \qquad \|\alpha_i\|=-i.$$
  - Explanation: Computes the rational homotopy algebra of the height-three local sphere as the stated exterior algebra.
- **claim-reduced-rank-three-building** (classification, [source](#stmt-h3-lem-rank-three-building)): Let $F$ be a non-Archimedean local field with normalized valuation $\nu$, valuation ring $\mathcal O$, uniformizer $\pi$, and residue field $\kappa$ of cardinality $q$. Let $\mathcal B$ be the reduced affine building of $\mathrm{GL}_3(F)$, equivalently the building of $\mathrm{PGL}_3(F)$, and put $$J_3(F)=\{g\in\mathrm{GL}_3(F):\nu(\det g)=0\}.$$ Then $\mathcal B$ is a contractible, locally finite, two-dimensional simplicial complex. Each vertex has $2(q^2+q+1)$ adjacent vertices. The group $J_3(F)$ preserves vertex types. The setwise stabilizer of every nonempty face is compact open in $J_3(F)$ and fixes that face pointwise. Any closed chamber is a fundamental domain, including all its faces.
  - Explanation: Identifies the reduced building's contractibility, dimension, local valency, type-preserving action, compact face stabilizers, and chamber fundamental domain.
- **claim-drinfeld-model-scalar-equivalence** (theorem, [source](#stmt-h3-lem-drinfeld-structure-sheaf)): Let $\mathfrak H$ be the $p$-adic completion of the standard separated strictly semistable weak formal model of $\Omega^2_{\mathbb Q_p}$ over $\mathbb Z_p$. The canonical scalar map $$\underline{\mathbb Z_p}\longrightarrow R\Gamma(\mathfrak H,\mathcal O)$$ is an equivalence of condensed complexes, and is equivariant for the action of $\mathop{\mathrm{GL}}_3(\mathbb Z_p)$. Here the right side retains the derived sections on $\mathfrak H\times\underline Q$ for every profinite set $Q$.
  - Explanation: Computes the formal Drinfeld model's structure-sheaf complex by its canonical scalar map, equivariantly and with every profinite parameter retained.

      "exact_statement": "Let $a:A\\to B$ be a map in a stable category, and let $L$ be an exact localization for which $La$ is an equivalence.         "exact_quote": "For $l\\geq1$, form the reduced closure of the locus of $r$ points of $\\mathcal G[p^l]$ whose images are a basis of the étale quotient at the generic point of $A_m$.           "exact_quote": "The support at the double origin in $N^2$ is a line in degree six, of scalar weight $-2$. The support in $D$ has cohomology in degrees three and five. In each degree it is a distribution module on $\\mathbb P^1(\\mathbb Q_p)$ with a one-dimensional continuous fiber. The scalar weights of these two fibers are respectively $-1$ and $-2$.*\n\n*These descriptions are equivariant relative descriptions, with continuous profinite parameters. For the stabilizer of the direction $(1,0)$, written $$B=\\left\\{\\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\\\0&d\\end{pmatrix}\n                \\in\\mathop{\\mathrm{GL}}_2(\\mathbb Z_p)\\right\\},$$ the two fibers have characters $\\bar d^{-1}$ and $\\bar a^{-1}\\bar d^{-1}$. An element $v\\in P_1=\\mathbb Z_p^\\times$ has characters $\\bar v$ and $\\bar v^2$, respectively. Normal Kummer twists are understood in these descriptions.",

        "exact_quote": "Let $q=|k|$, and let $M_k$ be the analytic function space over $k$ on a chosen perfected punctured ball or on the perfected ordinary polyannular open.         "anchor": "stmt-h3-thm-completed-cohomology",
        "exact_quote": "The completed strata of [h3:thm:coordinate-comparison](#h3:thm:coordinate-comparison) have the following properties.*\n\n1.  *For the ordinary completed coefficient ring $B_{\\mathrm{pk}}$, the natural constants map is an equivalence $$R\\Gamma_{\\mathrm{cts}}(\\mathop{\\mathrm{GL}}_2(\\mathbb Z_p)\\times P_1,k)\n       \\xrightarrow{\\ \\simeq\\ }\n     R\\Gamma_{\\mathrm{cts}}(P_3,B_{\\mathrm{pk}}).$$ It is the map defined by $Y_1\\to B(\\mathop{\\mathrm{GL}}_2(\\mathbb Z_p)\\times P_1)$, and is compatible with geometric constant extension, products, coefficient Frobenius, and profinite parameters. Every periodicity twist and finite tame character twist has finite cohomology in each degree, in a bounded range.*\n\n2.  *Let $L$ be the connected height-two marking algebra, $U\\subset P_2$ an open subgroup, $B=L^U$, and $B^{\\mathrm b}=\\widehat{B^{\\mathrm{perf}}}$. Finite products of fields are allowed. Then each $H^a_{\\mathrm{cts}}(H,B^{\\mathrm b})$ is finite-dimensional over $k$, and its degree-zero group is $k$ by constants. The same finiteness holds for lines framed on a finite connected-marking cover, including the periodicity and tame determinant lines used below. On taking the filtered colimit over marking levels there is a natural fiber sequence $$k\\longrightarrow\n     \\mathop{\\mathrm{colim}}_U R\\Gamma_{\\mathrm{cts}}(H,(L^U)^{\\mathrm b})\n       \\longrightarrow k_{\\lambda}[-3].$$ The first arrow is the inclusion of constants. The full residual norm quotient $P_3/H=\\mathbb Z_p^\\times$ acts on $k_\\lambda$ by $a\\mapsto\\bar a^{-2}$ in the point-action convention above. The commuting $P_2$ action is retained. It is smooth on the displayed finite-dimensional rows. The statement includes restrictions between marking levels. With a profinite parameter $T$, each displayed cohomology group is replaced by its $C_{\\mathrm{cts}}(T,-)$, as specified at the start of the section.*\n\n*In particular, invariants of the order-$p-1$ subgroup of the full norm quotient kill the extra line in <span class=\"upright\">(ii)</span>. This subgroup is in the quotient; no section of $P_3\\to\\mathbb Z_p^\\times$ is required.",
