      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-h3-co-compact-resolution",
        "exact_quote": "Let $G$ be a compact $p$-adic analytic group with no element of order $p$, and put $d=\\dim G$. The trivial module $\\mathbb F_p$ has a resolution of length $d$ by finitely generated projective $\\mathbb F_p[[G]]$-modules. For every complete linearly topologized representation $M$ with invariant neighborhoods, applying continuous $\\mathbb F_p[[G]]$-linear Hom to this resolution computes $C^\\bullet_{\\mathrm{cts}}(G,M)$ up to a continuous chain homotopy equivalence. Its terms are continuous direct summands of finite powers of $M$.*\n\n\n*If $M$ is compact, $H^a_{\\mathrm{cts}}(G,M)$ is compact Hausdorff. For $G=H$ or $G=P_3$, put $d_H=8$ and $d_{P_3}=9$. Their adjoint orientation characters are trivial, and there are natural identifications $$\\label{h3:co:compact-duality}\n H^a_{\\mathrm{cts}}(G,M)^\\vee\n \\cong H^{d_G-a}_{\\mathrm{cts}}(G,M^\\vee),\n \\qquad\n M^\\vee=\\mathop{\\mathrm{Hom}}_{\\mathrm{cts},\\mathbb F_p}(M,\\mathbb F_p),$$ where $M^\\vee$ has its discrete topology and contragredient action. The transposed coefficient map induces the dual cohomology map. The same formula, with compact and discrete sides interchanged, holds for a discrete continuous $\\mathbb F_p$-representation and its compact dual. In particular, finite coefficient modules have finite cohomology.",
        "source_id": "PM-318.2"
      },
      "evidence": [
        {
          "anchor": "stmt-h3-co-compact-resolution",
          "exact_quote": "Let $G$ be a compact $p$-adic analytic group with no element of order $p$, and put $d=\\dim G$. The trivial module $\\mathbb F_p$ has a resolution of length $d$ by finitely generated projective $\\mathbb F_p[[G]]$-modules. For every complete linearly topologized representation $M$ with invariant neighborhoods, applying continuous $\\mathbb F_p[[G]]$-linear Hom to this resolution computes $C^\\bullet_{\\mathrm{cts}}(G,M)$ up to a continuous chain homotopy equivalence. Its terms are continuous direct summands of finite powers of $M$.*\n\n\n*If $M$ is compact, $H^a_{\\mathrm{cts}}(G,M)$ is compact Hausdorff. For $G=H$ or $G=P_3$, put $d_H=8$ and $d_{P_3}=9$. Their adjoint orientation characters are trivial, and there are natural identifications $$\\label{h3:co:compact-duality}\n H^a_{\\mathrm{cts}}(G,M)^\\vee\n \\cong H^{d_G-a}_{\\mathrm{cts}}(G,M^\\vee),\n \\qquad\n M^\\vee=\\mathop{\\mathrm{Hom}}_{\\mathrm{cts},\\mathbb F_p}(M,\\mathbb F_p),$$ where $M^\\vee$ has its discrete topology and contragredient action. The transposed coefficient map induces the dual cohomology map. The same formula, with compact and discrete sides interchanged, holds for a discrete continuous $\\mathbb F_p$-representation and its compact dual. In particular, finite coefficient modules have finite cohomology.",

      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-h3-co-strictness",
        "exact_quote": "Let $A^\\bullet$ be a complex of Polish abelian groups with continuous differentials. If $H^a(A^\\bullet)$ is finite, its quotient topology is discrete. More precisely, the boundary subgroup $B^a$ is open and closed in the cycle group $Z^a$, and $\\partial:A^{a-1}\\twoheadrightarrow B^a$ is open. Consequently, for every neighborhood $V$ of zero in $A^{a-1}$ there is a neighborhood $W$ of zero in $Z^a$ such that every member of $W$ has a primitive in $V$.",

      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-h3-co-parameters",
        "exact_quote": "Let $T$ be a profinite space.*\n\n1.  *A continuous map $T\\to F$ lifts through every continuous open surjective homomorphism $E\\twoheadrightarrow F$ of Polish abelian groups.*\n\n2.  *If a Polish complex $A^\\bullet$ has finite cohomology in every degree, then $$H^a C(T,A^\\bullet)\\cong C(T,H^a(A^\\bullet)),$$ where the finite cohomology group on the right is discrete.*\n\n3.  *For a filtered system of such complexes, the corresponding identity commutes with the cochain colimit, with the colimit of the cohomology groups given its discrete topology.",

        "exact_quote": "After a finite enlargement of $k$, the inverse-limit distribution algebra of <a href=\"#h3:co:root-torsors\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"h3:co:root-torsors\">[h3:co:root-torsors]</a> is $k[[D]]$, with a parameter $D$ having the following properties.*\n\n1.  *It acts $L$-linearly and locally nilpotently on $R$. For every $i\\geq0$, $$\\ker(D^{p^i}:R\\to R)=L^{1/p^i}.$$ It is surjective, and $D^{p^i-1}:L^{1/p^i}\\to L$ is nonzero on every factor.*\n\n\n2.  *It commutes with $H$. Its residual $\\mu_{p-1}$-character is $\\chi(u)=u^{s_{\\mathrm{dist}}}$, where $s_{\\mathrm{dist}}\\in\\{1,-1\\}$. Thus $$\\label{h3:co:distribution-sequence}\n     0\\longrightarrow L\\longrightarrow R\n     \\xrightarrow{D} R(\\chi^{-1})\\longrightarrow0$$ is an exact sequence of $H'$-modules.*\n\n\n3.  *If $q=p^i$, where $i$ is even and divisible by $[k:\\mathbb F_p]$, then $$\\label{h3:co:frobenius-distribution}\n     D(f^q)=(D^qf)^q,\\qquad\n     D^q(z^{1/q})=(Dz)^{1/q}.$$ In particular $D^q$ is $L^{1/q}$-linear.*\n\n4.  *On any complete finite separable and root stage these operators are continuous after passage to a larger such stage. Each target stage admits a continuous additive right inverse of $D$ with values in one larger stage.         "anchor": "stmt-h3-lem-exact-amitsur",
        "exact_quote": "Let $\\mathcal C$ be a stable symmetric monoidal $\\infty$-category with limits and with tensor product exact in each variable. Let $E$ be a descendable commutative algebra, write $\\mathbf1$ for the unit, and put $I_E=\\mathop{\\mathrm{fib}}(\\mathbf1\\to E)$. For its full Amitsur object $C^q=E^{\\otimes(q+1)}$, the partial totalization $$\\operatorname{Tot}_s C^\\bullet\n   =\\lim_{[q]\\in\\Delta_{\\leq s}}C^q$$ is a finite cubical limit. Its augmentation fiber, including its map to the unit, is $$\\label{h3:des:partial-amitsur-fiber}\n \\bigl(\\mathop{\\mathrm{fib}}(\\mathbf1\\longrightarrow\\operatorname{Tot}_s C^\\bullet)\n       \\longrightarrow\\mathbf1\\bigr)\n \\simeq \\bigl(I_E^{\\otimes(s+1)}\\longrightarrow\\mathbf1\\bigr).$$ The transition between successive fibers applies $I_E\\to\\mathbf1$ to the last factor. There is an integer $N$ such that every composite of $N$ successive maps between these augmentation fibers is null. Every exact functor from $\\mathcal C$ to a stable category preserves the augmented totalization $\\mathbf1\\simeq\\operatorname{Tot}C^\\bullet$ and this same null-composite bound.",
        "source_id": "PM-318.2"
      },
      "evidence": [
        {
          "anchor": "stmt-h3-lem-exact-amitsur",
          "exact_quote": "Let $\\mathcal C$ be a stable symmetric monoidal $\\infty$-category with limits and with tensor product exact in each variable. Let $E$ be a descendable commutative algebra, write $\\mathbf1$ for the unit, and put $I_E=\\mathop{\\mathrm{fib}}(\\mathbf1\\to E)$. For its full Amitsur object $C^q=E^{\\otimes(q+1)}$, the partial totalization $$\\operatorname{Tot}_s C^\\bullet\n   =\\lim_{[q]\\in\\Delta_{\\leq s}}C^q$$ is a finite cubical limit. Its augmentation fiber, including its map to the unit, is $$\\label{h3:des:partial-amitsur-fiber}\n \\bigl(\\mathop{\\mathrm{fib}}(\\mathbf1\\longrightarrow\\operatorname{Tot}_s C^\\bullet)\n       \\longrightarrow\\mathbf1\\bigr)\n \\simeq \\bigl(I_E^{\\otimes(s+1)}\\longrightarrow\\mathbf1\\bigr).$$ The transition between successive fibers applies $I_E\\to\\mathbf1$ to the last factor. There is an integer $N$ such that every composite of $N$ successive maps between these augmentation fibers is null. Every exact functor from $\\mathcal C$ to a stable category preserves the augmented totalization $\\mathbf1\\simeq\\operatorname{Tot}C^\\bullet$ and this same null-composite bound.",
          "source_id": "PM-318.2"
        }
      ],
      "exact_statement": "Let $\\mathcal C$ be a stable symmetric monoidal $\\infty$-category with limits and with tensor product exact in each variable. Let $E$ be a descendable commutative algebra, write $\\mathbf1$ for the unit, and put $I_E=\\mathop{\\mathrm{fib}}(\\mathbf1\\to E)$. For its full Amitsur object $C^q=E^{\\otimes(q+1)}$, the partial totalization $$\\operatorname{Tot}_s C^\\bullet\n   =\\lim_{[q]\\in\\Delta_{\\leq s}}C^q$$ is a finite cubical limit. Its augmentation fiber, including its map to the unit, is $$\\label{h3:des:partial-amitsur-fiber}\n \\bigl(\\mathop{\\mathrm{fib}}(\\mathbf1\\longrightarrow\\operatorname{Tot}_s C^\\bullet)\n       \\longrightarrow\\mathbf1\\bigr)\n \\simeq \\bigl(I_E^{\\otimes(s+1)}\\longrightarrow\\mathbf1\\bigr).$$ The transition between successive fibers applies $I_E\\to\\mathbf1$ to the last factor. There is an integer $N$ such that every composite of $N$ successive maps between these augmentation fibers is null. Every exact functor from $\\mathcal C$ to a stable category preserves the augmented totalization $\\mathbf1\\simeq\\operatorname{Tot}C^\\bullet$ and this same null-composite bound.",

        "anchor": "stmt-h3-prop-exact-descent",
        "exact_quote": "Let $n\\geq1$, let $k$ be a finite field containing $F=\\mathbb F_{p^n}$, and let $R_{n,k}=L_{K(n)}S_k$. In the $K(n)$-local category of $S_k$-modules, the algebra $E_n(k)$ is descendable over the unit $R_{n,k}$. Write $\\widehat\\otimes$ for the tensor product in this local category and put $$\\mathcal N_n^q=E_n(k)^{\\widehat\\otimes_{R_{n,k}}(q+1)}\n \\qquad(q\\geq0).$$ Its augmented Amitsur object totalizes to $R_{n,k}$. Every exact functor from this local category to a stable category preserves that totalization and a uniform nilpotence bound for its error tower. In particular this applies to the inclusion in spectra followed by ordinary smash, a finite Moore quotient, a chromatic localization, or a monochromatic fiber.*\n\n\n*There are identifications of graded rings $$\\label{h3:des:relative-cooperations}\n \\pi_*\\mathcal N_n^q\n    \\cong C_{\\mathrm{cts}}(P_n^q,E_n(k)_*),$$ with the maximal-ideal topology on the coefficients. Under these identifications the actual cofaces and codegeneracies induce those of the continuous action cobar construction, and the augmented unit is the constant unit. Each $\\mathcal N_n^q$ is an ordinary $E_n(k)$-module through its first factor. This is the module structure used when an ordinary exact functor is applied to a term.",

      },

        "exact_quote": "There is a continuous $G$-equivariant $B_0$-linear retraction $B_0^{1/p}\\to B_0$. All these maps are compatible with constant-field descent.",

        "anchor": "stmt-h3-ord-loss-bounds",
        "exact_quote": "Fix the operators of [h3:ord:root-retractions](#h3:ord:root-retractions) and a free rational frame of $\\mathcal L$, using the normalized Gauss valuations just specified. There are constants $c\\geq0$ and $c_{a,b}\\geq0$ such that $$\\begin{aligned}\n \\mathcal P(A_L(\\mathcal L))\n   &\\subseteq A_{L/q+c}(\\mathcal L),\\label{h3:ord:one-pole-bound}\\\\\n v_{a,b}(\\mathcal Pf)\n   &\\geq q^{-1}v_{a,b}(f)-c_{a,b}.\n   \\label{h3:ord:one-norm-bound}\n\\end{aligned}$$ For real indices the pole inequality defines the lattice, so $A_t=A_{\\lfloor t\\rfloor}$ in the original integral frame. With $C=c/(1-q^{-1})$ and $C_{a,b}=c_{a,b}/(1-q^{-1})$, iteration gives $$\\begin{aligned}\n \\mathcal P^n(A_L(\\mathcal L))\n   &\\subseteq A_{q^{-n}L+C}(\\mathcal L),\\label{h3:ord:iterated-poles}\\\\\n v_{a,b}(\\mathcal P^nf)\n   &\\geq q^{-n}v_{a,b}(f)-C_{a,b}.\n   \\label{h3:ord:iterated-norms}\n\\end{aligned}$$ The losses for $\\rho_n$ in <a href=\"#h3:ord:finite-root-projection\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"h3:ord:finite-root-projection\">[h3:ord:finite-root-projection]</a> are therefore independent of the root level.",

        "anchor": "stmt-h3-des-unit-directions",
        "exact_quote": "Under the natural ordinary coefficient comparison, the map from the height-one sphere sends its degree-minus-one mod-$p$ generator to the connected logarithm $h$.       },
      "evidence": [

          "anchor": "stmt-h3-des-unit-directions",
          "exact_quote": "Under the natural ordinary coefficient comparison, the map from the height-one sphere sends its degree-minus-one mod-$p$ generator to the connected logarithm $h$.         }

        "anchor": "stmt-h3-des-finite-length-model",
        "exact_quote": "The ordinary spectrum $L_1(T/p^\\ell)$ is the totalization of the termwise $L_1(-/p^\\ell)$ Morava descent object. The corresponding spectral sequence is strongly convergent, has columns $0\\leq s\\leq5$, and has no differentials. All its abutment groups are finite in each stem.         "anchor": "stmt-h3-rat-finite-classifying",
        "exact_quote": "For a $G$-space $X$ over $B$ there is a natural finite coefficient map $$\\label{h3:eq:rat-finite-classifying}\n \\mathsf u_{X,G,\\ell}:\n C^\\bullet_{\\mathrm{cts}}(G,\\Lambda_\\ell)\n \\longrightarrow\n \\operatorname{Tot}_{[a]\\in\\Delta}\n R\\Gamma_v(X\\times\\underline{G^a},\\Lambda_\\ell)\n \\simeq R\\Gamma_v([X/G],\\Lambda_\\ell).$$ For a $G$-torsor $T\\to Z$ over $B$ with relative classifying map $c_T:Z\\to\\mathrm B_B G$, this gives $$\\operatorname{cl}_{c_T,\\ell}\n   :=c_T^*\\mathsf u_{B,G,\\ell}:\n C^\\bullet_{\\mathrm{cts}}(G,\\Lambda_\\ell)\n       \\longrightarrow R\\Gamma_v(Z,\\Lambda_\\ell).$$ It equals <a href=\"#h3:eq:rat-finite-classifying\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"h3:eq:rat-finite-classifying\">[h3:eq:rat-finite-classifying]</a> for $X=T$ under $[T/G]\\simeq Z$. Their derived coefficient limits and their rationalizations define maps denoted $\\operatorname{cl}_{c_T,\\mathrm{int}}$ and $\\operatorname{cl}_{c_T,\\mathrm b}$ on the corresponding cohomology.*\n\n\n*For an algebraically closed perfectoid field $C$ of characteristic zero, put $B_C=\\operatorname{Spa}(C,\\mathcal O_C)^\\diamond$.         "anchor": "stmt-h3-rat-solid-resolution",
        "exact_quote": "The complexes $\\mathscr C_Z$ are bounded below, derived solid, and derived $p$-complete. Let $G$ be a compact $p$-adic analytic group without $p$-torsion. There is a finite projective resolution $P_\\bullet\\to\\mathbb Z_p$ over $\\Lambda_G=\\mathbb Z_p[[G]]$, with finitely generated terms and length $\\dim G$, such that, for every derived solid $\\underline{\\mathbb Z_p}$-module complex $K$ with $\\underline{\\mathbb Z_p}$-linear continuous $G$-action, $$\\label{h3:eq:rat-solid-hom}\n R\\Gamma(G,K)(*)\\simeq\\mathop{\\mathrm{Hom}}_{\\Lambda_G}(P_\\bullet,K).$$ Here $\\mathop{\\mathrm{Hom}}$ is the external complex of morphisms in solid $\\underline{\\Lambda_G}$-modules. A continuous action means an actual module over $\\underline{\\mathbb Z_p}[\\underline G]$ in the derived condensed category, rather than an action on $K(*)$. If $K$ is bounded below, and an operator $\\gamma$ commuting with $G$ acts by the scalar $\\lambda_j\\in\\mathbb Q_p$ on $H^j(K)(*)[1/p]$, it acts by $\\lambda_j$ on $H^s(G,H^j(K))(*)[1/p]$ for every $s$. For $K=\\mathscr C_Z$ the resulting spectral sequence is $$\\label{h3:eq:rat-solid-descent}\n H^s(G,H^j(\\mathscr C_Z))(*)[1/p]\n       \\ \\Longrightarrow\\ H^{s+j}_{\\mathrm b}([Z/G]),$$ with a finite filtration in each total degree.",
        "source_id": "PM-318.2"
      },

<a id="pm-s2"></a>
## 2. Definitions, validity and bounds

- **Height-three overlap and local units** ([source](#pm-h-11)): We work with $p$-local spectra and write $$S=\mathbb S_p^\wedge,\qquad T=L_{K(3)}S,\qquad X=L_2T,\qquad R_i=L_{K(i)}S.$$
- **Ordered homotopy filtration** ([source](#pm-h-3)): A filtration means a sequence of homotopy cofiber sequences: its $i$-th cofiber $C_i$ has a connecting map $\partial_i:C_i\to\Sigma F_{i-1}$.
- **Local-sphere blocks** ([source](#pm-h-4)): Put $Q=L_0S\simeq H\mathbb Q_p$, and group the layers as $$\begin{aligned} W&=L_2S\vee\Sigma^{-1}L_2S,\\ U_{\mathrm{mid}}&=\Sigma^{-3}L_1S\vee\Sigma^{-4}L_1S,\\ V&=\Sigma^{-5}Q\vee\Sigma^{-6}Q \vee\Sigma^{-8}Q\vee\Sigma^{-9}Q. \end{aligned}$$
- **Morava deformation coefficients** ([source](#pm-h-11)): At height three our coefficient convention is $$E_{3,*}(k)=W(k)[[x,y]][u^{\pm1}],\qquad \|u\|=-2.$$
- **Periodicity line** ([source](#pm-h-11)): The invariant cotangent, or periodicity, line is $\omega=\pi_2E_3(k)$; it is generated by $u^{-1}$ over the degree-zero ring.
- **Algebraic ordinary coefficient ring** ([source](#pm-h-11)): Set $$A=k[[x,y]],\qquad x=u_1,\quad y=u_2,\qquad B_0=A[x^{-1}].$$
- **Honda stabilizer** ([source](#pm-h-12)): Let $D_n$ be the central division algebra over $\mathbb Q_p$ of invariant $1/n$, and let $$P_n=\mathcal O_{D_n}^{\times}.$$
- **Reduced-norm kernel and tame preimage** ([source](#pm-h-12)): At height three, define $$H=\ker\bigl(\mathop{\mathrm{Nrd}}:P_3\to\mathbb Z_p^\times\bigr),\qquad H'=\mathop{\mathrm{Nrd}}^{-1}(\mu_{p-1}).$$
- **Continuous cochain complex** ([source](#pm-h-13)): For a topological group $G$ and a continuous coefficient module $M$, we use the inhomogeneous continuous cochain complex $$C^q_{\mathrm{cts}}(G,M)=C_{\mathrm{cts}}(G^q,M)$$ with its usual differential.
- **Filtered coefficient cochain convention** ([source](#pm-h-13)): If $M=\mathop{\mathrm{colim}}_\lambda M_\lambda$ is such a coefficient object, our notation means $$\label{h3:eq:framework-filtered-cochains} C^\bullet_{\mathrm{cts}}(G,M) :=\mathop{\mathrm{colim}}_\lambda C^\bullet_{\mathrm{cts}}(G,M_\lambda).$$
- **Basic positive bundle** ([source](#pm-h-14)): Let $$V_s=\mathcal O(1/s)$$ be the stable rank-$s$, degree-one bundle.
- **Perfected Honda open ball** ([source](#h3:sec:towers)): The notation $H_s$ denotes the perfected open Honda ball: on an affinoid perfectoid $k$-algebra $(R,R^+)$ it is $R^{\circ\circ}$, with addition defined by $\Gamma_s$.
- **Independent Honda tuples** ([source](#pm-h-17)): $$ For a compatible sequence $(t_j)$, consecutive terms in the second formula differ by at most $\lambda^{q^j}$. Its limit $z$ satisfies $\|z-t_j^{q^j}\|\leq\lambda^{q^j}$. Substitution in the first formula and the displayed contraction show in both directions that the formulas are inverse. This reasoning never requires a common strict upper bound on all the $\|t_j\|$. The coefficients of $\Gamma_3$ are fixed by the $q$th-power map. The difference between the two addition laws is at most $\lambda$; after $n$ applications of $P_a$ it is at most $\lambda^{d^n}$. Taking the limit proves additivity. If $g$ changes the deformation framing, its evaluated coordinate change differs from its Honda reduction by coefficients of norm at most $\lambda$, after increasing $\lambda$ if necessary. The same contraction proves $\Phi_{ga}(gz)=g\Phi_a(z)$. Uniform convergence on smaller balls proves continuity and compatibility with maps of perfectoid algebras. Over an algebraically closed field the points with $t_0=0$ are exactly the compatible $p^j$-torsion points. A finite connected group over a perfect field has just its identity as a geometric point, so these points form the Tate module of the étale quotient. The zeroth projection is surjective: preparation applied to $[p](T)-w$ gives a monic distinguished polynomial, each of whose roots is small when $w$ is small. Successively choosing roots gives a compatible sequence with prescribed $t_0$. ◻ </details> Write $(H_3^r)_{\mathrm{ind}}$ for the locus of tuples whose images on every geometric fiber are $\mathbb Q_p$-linearly independent for the Honda vector-space structure on $H_3$.
- **Integral determinant-lattice structure** ([source](#pm-h-19)): A $P_s$-structured form of $V_s$ is a form whose $D_s^\times$-torsor of frames has been reduced to $P_s$.
- **Locally finite distributions** ([source](#h3:ana:distribution-definition)): For a compact totally disconnected space $K$ define $$\mathcal D(K,R)= \varprojlim_{\mathscr P}\bigoplus_{U\in\mathscr P}R, \qquad (a_V)_{V\in\mathscr Q}\longmapsto \left(\sum_{V\subset U}a_V\right)_{U\in\mathscr P}, \tag{$\ast$}\label{h3:ana:distribution-definition}$$ where $\mathscr Q$ refines the finite clopen partition $\mathscr P$.
- **Coheight-one Cartier operator** ([source](#pm-h-28)): We write $\mathrm{Car}$ for Cartier on differentials and set $$\label{h3:co:cartier-definition} \mathcal C(f)=\frac{\mathrm{Car}(f\eta)}{\eta}.$$
- **Order lattice** ([source](#pm-h-29)): An order lattice in a finite product of local fields means a product of fractional powers of their maximal ideals.
- **Descendable commutative algebra** ([source](#pm-h-33)): A commutative algebra is *descendable* if the unit belongs to the thick tensor ideal it generates.
- **Holomorphic ordinary coefficients** ([source](#pm-h-37)): The ring $B_{\mathrm{hol}}$ consists of the integral-exponent series for which, for every $a,b>0$ and every real $N$, only finitely many nonzero terms have $ai+bj\leq N$.
- **Compact ordinary pole lattices** ([source](#pm-h-37)): Write $\mathcal L$ for such a line, with its original free $A$-lattice $\mathcal L_A$, and set $$A_d(\mathcal L)=x^{-d}\mathcal L_A\quad(d\in\mathbb Z), \qquad B_{\mathrm{hol}}(\mathcal L)=B_{\mathrm{hol}}\otimes_A\mathcal L_A, \qquad B_{\mathrm{pk}}(\mathcal L)=B_{\mathrm{pk}}\otimes_A\mathcal L_A.$$
- **Finite-length ordinary coefficients** ([source](#pm-h-44)): Put $$A_\ell=(W(k)/p^\ell)[[x,y]],\qquad D_\ell=A_\ell[x^{-1}].$$
- **Integral geometric and bounded rational cohomology** ([source](#pm-h-47)): For a small v-stack $Z$ in this section, set $$R\Gamma_{\mathrm{int}}(Z) =R\varprojlim_{\ell}R\Gamma_v(Z,\Lambda_\ell),\qquad H^i_{\mathrm{int}}(Z)=H^i(R\Gamma_{\mathrm{int}}(Z)), \qquad H^i_{\mathrm b}(Z)=H^i_{\mathrm{int}}(Z)[1/p].$$
- **Canonical rationalized height-two map** ([source](#pm-h-55)): Let $$u_X:L_0X\longrightarrow L_0L_{K(2)}X$$ be induced by the canonical localization unit.

<a id="pm-s3"></a>
## 3. Proof roadmap

- **step-boundary-sign** [claim](#stmt-lem-boundary) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-boundary): Compare cofiber sequences under the source and use the fixed rotation convention. -> The signed localization-boundary formula.
- **step-fracture-assembly** [claim](#stmt-prop-fracture) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-fracture): Glue the middle map by fracture, pull back ordered partial sums, and identify the terminal rational quotient. -> The ordered filtration and terminal equivalence.
- **step-attachment-roofs** [claim](#stmt-thm-attachment-identification) / [proof](#proof-stmt-thm-attachment-identification): Collect the boundaries and signed roofs already proved for the same construction. -> Attachment formulas for the chosen filtration.
- **step-group-foundations** [claim](#stmt-h3-lem-framework-groups) / [proof](#proof-stmt-h3-lem-framework-groups): Exclude prime torsion by subfield and representation degrees, compute Lie dimensions and orientations, and construct finite resolutions. -> Finite cohomological dimensions and projective resolutions.
- **step-semilinear-contraction** [claim](#stmt-h3-lem-framework-semilinear) / [proof](#proof-stmt-h3-lem-framework-semilinear): Use a trace-one element to project semilinear modules and contract higher cochains. -> Exact finite-field descent.
- **step-regular-torsion-coordinates** [claim](#stmt-h3-geom-regular-levels) / [proof](#proof-stmt-h3-geom-regular-levels): Use preparation, the basis divisor, and maximal-ideal dimension arguments to identify finite coordinate rings and transitions. -> Regular finite-level basis and lift algebras.
- **step-cover-contraction** [claim](#stmt-h3-geom-universal-cover) / [proof](#proof-stmt-h3-geom-universal-cover): Compare successive normalized division coordinates by contraction and verify additivity and framing naturality. -> Natural inverse universal-cover coordinates.
- **step-coordinate-norm-comparison** [claim](#stmt-h3-thm-coordinate-comparison) / [proof](#proof-stmt-h3-thm-coordinate-comparison): Pass finite coordinate algebras through completed perfection using uniform spectral estimates and identify the independent locus. -> Equivariant completed Tate-coordinate comparison.
- **step-relative-bundle-inputs** [claim](#stmt-h3-geom-curve-inputs) / [proof](#proof-stmt-h3-geom-curve-inputs): Identify universal covers with relative sections and use relative bundle classification, vanishing, and full faithfulness. -> Section, frame, and relative morphism comparisons.
- **step-independent-extensions** [claim](#stmt-h3-geom-independent-extensions) / [proof](#proof-stmt-h3-geom-independent-extensions): Use stability and integral degrees to classify subbundles and detect split quotients by linear functionals. -> The independent extension locus.
- **step-integral-frames** [claim](#stmt-h3-prop-integral-frames) / [proof](#proof-stmt-h3-prop-integral-frames): Retain connected markings and integral Tate bases, normalize determinant lattices, and compare the resulting frame torsors. -> Frame-stack equivalence and normalized marking tower.
- **step-uniform-etale-descent** [claim](#stmt-h3-geom-uniform-etale-descent) / [proof](#proof-stmt-h3-geom-uniform-etale-descent): Descend idempotents and simple roots by uniform approximation and Hensel lifting in a common complete finite product. -> Finite-stage descent of every specified section.
- **step-algebraic-markings** [claim](#stmt-h3-lem-marking-descent) / [proof](#proof-stmt-h3-lem-marking-descent): Descend normalized finite étale generators, identify their radicial lift algebras, and pass finite torsor identities to limits. -> Algebraic root torsors and completed finite-level quotient stacks.
- **step-canonical-differential** [claim](#stmt-h3-lem-invariant-differential) / [proof](#proof-stmt-h3-lem-invariant-differential): Apply the canonical-line theorem and conormal sequence, then transport the Honda invariant differential through the connected marking. -> A finite-stage norm-kernel invariant differential.
- **step-ordinary-splitting-torsor** [claim](#stmt-h3-lem-ordinary-torsor) / [proof](#proof-stmt-h3-lem-ordinary-torsor): Identify splittings on an étale basis cover with all generator lifts and descend the canonical root algebra. -> Natural multiplicative-type root torsors over algebraic ordinary coefficients.
- **step-additive-negative-presentation** [claim](#stmt-h3-ana-relative-bc) / [proof](#proof-stmt-h3-ana-relative-bc): Take relative sections of the untilt-divisor sequence after unramified pushforward. -> The additive quotient presentation of the negative extension space.
- **step-kummer-restriction** [claim](#stmt-h3-ana-annulus-contraction) / [proof](#proof-stmt-h3-ana-annulus-contraction): Divide nonzero fractional monomials by the Kummer difference eigenvalues after imposing the radius gaps. -> A uniformly bounded nonconstant contracting homotopy.

          "exact_quote": "For $l\\geq1$, form the reduced closure of the locus of $r$ points of $\\mathcal G[p^l]$ whose images are a basis of the étale quotient at the generic point of $A_m$. Its coordinate algebra $B_l$ is finite over $A_m$, and its lifted point coordinates $t_{1,l},\\ldots,t_{r,l}$ give isomorphisms $$B_l=k[[t_{1,l},\\ldots,t_{r,l}]],\\qquad\n C_l:=A_m[t_{1,l}^{p^{ml}},\\ldots,t_{r,l}^{p^{ml}}]\n     =k[[t_{1,l}^{p^{ml}},\\ldots,t_{r,l}^{p^{ml}}]].$$ The subalgebra on the left is already complete. The algebra $C_l[u_m^{-1}]$ is the finite étale algebra of bases of $\\mathcal G^{\\mathrm{et}}[p^l]$ over $A_m[u_m^{-1}]$. Over this basis cover, $B_l[u_m^{-1}]$ is the algebra of all generator lifts, without taking a reduction. The transition maps $B_j\\to B_l$, $j\\leq l$, are finite injective maps, and $$t_{i,j}\\in\n k[[t_{1,l}^{p^{m(l-j)}},\\ldots,t_{r,l}^{p^{m(l-j)}}]].$$",

          "anchor": "stmt-h3-thm-completed-cohomology",
          "exact_quote": "The completed strata of [h3:thm:coordinate-comparison](#h3:thm:coordinate-comparison) have the following properties.*\n\n1.  *For the ordinary completed coefficient ring $B_{\\mathrm{pk}}$, the natural constants map is an equivalence $$R\\Gamma_{\\mathrm{cts}}(\\mathop{\\mathrm{GL}}_2(\\mathbb Z_p)\\times P_1,k)\n       \\xrightarrow{\\ \\simeq\\ }\n     R\\Gamma_{\\mathrm{cts}}(P_3,B_{\\mathrm{pk}}).$$ It is the map defined by $Y_1\\to B(\\mathop{\\mathrm{GL}}_2(\\mathbb Z_p)\\times P_1)$, and is compatible with geometric constant extension, products, coefficient Frobenius, and profinite parameters. Every periodicity twist and finite tame character twist has finite cohomology in each degree, in a bounded range.*\n\n2.  *Let $L$ be the connected height-two marking algebra, $U\\subset P_2$ an open subgroup, $B=L^U$, and $B^{\\mathrm b}=\\widehat{B^{\\mathrm{perf}}}$. Finite products of fields are allowed. Then each $H^a_{\\mathrm{cts}}(H,B^{\\mathrm b})$ is finite-dimensional over $k$, and its degree-zero group is $k$ by constants. The same finiteness holds for lines framed on a finite connected-marking cover, including the periodicity and tame determinant lines used below. On taking the filtered colimit over marking levels there is a natural fiber sequence $$k\\longrightarrow\n     \\mathop{\\mathrm{colim}}_U R\\Gamma_{\\mathrm{cts}}(H,(L^U)^{\\mathrm b})\n       \\longrightarrow k_{\\lambda}[-3].$$ The first arrow is the inclusion of constants. The full residual norm quotient $P_3/H=\\mathbb Z_p^\\times$ acts on $k_\\lambda$ by $a\\mapsto\\bar a^{-2}$ in the point-action convention above. The commuting $P_2$ action is retained. It is smooth on the displayed finite-dimensional rows. The statement includes restrictions between marking levels. With a profinite parameter $T$, each displayed cohomology group is replaced by its $C_{\\mathrm{cts}}(T,-)$, as specified at the start of the section.*\n\n*In particular, invariants of the order-$p-1$ subgroup of the full norm quotient kill the extra line in <span class=\"upright\">(ii)</span>. This subgroup is in the quotient; no section of $P_3\\to\\mathbb Z_p^\\times$ is required.",

          "anchor": "stmt-h3-co-compact-resolution",
          "exact_quote": "Let $G$ be a compact $p$-adic analytic group with no element of order $p$, and put $d=\\dim G$. The trivial module $\\mathbb F_p$ has a resolution of length $d$ by finitely generated projective $\\mathbb F_p[[G]]$-modules. For every complete linearly topologized representation $M$ with invariant neighborhoods, applying continuous $\\mathbb F_p[[G]]$-linear Hom to this resolution computes $C^\\bullet_{\\mathrm{cts}}(G,M)$ up to a continuous chain homotopy equivalence. Its terms are continuous direct summands of finite powers of $M$.*\n\n\n*If $M$ is compact, $H^a_{\\mathrm{cts}}(G,M)$ is compact Hausdorff. For $G=H$ or $G=P_3$, put $d_H=8$ and $d_{P_3}=9$. Their adjoint orientation characters are trivial, and there are natural identifications $$\\label{h3:co:compact-duality}\n H^a_{\\mathrm{cts}}(G,M)^\\vee\n \\cong H^{d_G-a}_{\\mathrm{cts}}(G,M^\\vee),\n \\qquad\n M^\\vee=\\mathop{\\mathrm{Hom}}_{\\mathrm{cts},\\mathbb F_p}(M,\\mathbb F_p),$$ where $M^\\vee$ has its discrete topology and contragredient action. The transposed coefficient map induces the dual cohomology map. The same formula, with compact and discrete sides interchanged, holds for a discrete continuous $\\mathbb F_p$-representation and its compact dual. In particular, finite coefficient modules have finite cohomology.",
          "source_id": "PM-318.2"
        }

          "anchor": "stmt-h3-lem-exact-amitsur",
          "exact_quote": "Let $\\mathcal C$ be a stable symmetric monoidal $\\infty$-category with limits and with tensor product exact in each variable. For its full Amitsur object $C^q=E^{\\otimes(q+1)}$, the partial totalization $$\\operatorname{Tot}_s C^\\bullet\n   =\\lim_{[q]\\in\\Delta_{\\leq s}}C^q$$ is a finite cubical limit. Its augmentation fiber, including its map to the unit, is $$\\label{h3:des:partial-amitsur-fiber}\n \\bigl(\\mathop{\\mathrm{fib}}(\\mathbf1\\longrightarrow\\operatorname{Tot}_s C^\\bullet)\n       \\longrightarrow\\mathbf1\\bigr)\n \\simeq \\bigl(I_E^{\\otimes(s+1)}\\longrightarrow\\mathbf1\\bigr).$$ The transition between successive fibers applies $I_E\\to\\mathbf1$ to the last factor. There is an integer $N$ such that every composite of $N$ successive maps between these augmentation fibers is null. Every exact functor from $\\mathcal C$ to a stable category preserves the augmented totalization $\\mathbf1\\simeq\\operatorname{Tot}C^\\bullet$ and this same null-composite bound.",
          "source_id": "PM-318.2"
        }

Write $\\widehat\\otimes$ for the tensor product in this local category and put $$\\mathcal N_n^q=E_n(k)^{\\widehat\\otimes_{R_{n,k}}(q+1)}\n \\qquad(q\\geq0).$$ Its augmented Amitsur object totalizes to $R_{n,k}$. Every exact functor from this local category to a stable category preserves that totalization and a uniform nilpotence bound for its error tower. In particular this applies to the inclusion in spectra followed by ordinary smash, a finite Moore quotient, a chromatic localization, or a monochromatic fiber.*\n\n\n*There are identifications of graded rings $$\\label{h3:des:relative-cooperations}\n \\pi_*\\mathcal N_n^q\n    \\cong C_{\\mathrm{cts}}(P_n^q,E_n(k)_*),$$ with the maximal-ideal topology on the coefficients. Each $\\mathcal N_n^q$ is an ordinary $E_n(k)$-module through its first factor. This is the module structure used when an ordinary exact functor is applied to a term.",

<a id="pm-s4"></a>
## 4. Engineering Triptych

### Panel 1 - epistemic contract

- **invariant-canonical-unit-filtration**: The ordered filtration has the stated local-sphere cofibers, its terminal projection is an equivalence, and its first-stage composite is the canonical unit.
- **invariant-choice-dependent-attachments**: The connecting maps and both signed roofs identify attachments of the same filtration only with the specified local maps, compatibility homotopy, and coherent inverse data.
- **invariant-bounded-stage-cochains**: Algebraic coefficient unions are interpreted through filtered colimits of cochain complexes, so each cochain retains a common finite stage or pole bound.
- **invariant-common-rational-scalar**: The actual rationalized localization carries the primitive and its determinant product with the same nonzero scalar, permitting a compatible rational normalization for fracture.
- **invariant-nonzero-middle-attachment**: For the common height-three realization, the first height-one connecting map is nonzero as a map of underlying spectra.

### Panel 2 - negative knowledge

- **anti-use-unrestricted-primes**: Apply the stated height-three filtration at every prime. -> This extends the result beyond its stated prime range and the group-theoretic hypotheses used in the coefficient comparisons.
- **anti-use-canonical-attachments**: Treat every attachment and stage as canonical or uniquely determined. -> The realization depends on the compatibility homotopy and coherent inverses.
- **anti-use-wedge-from-cofibers**: Replace the constructed filtration by a wedge of its cofibers. -> The first height-one attachment is nonzero for the stated realization, so its extension cannot be discarded.
- **anti-use-dimension-only-gluing**: Construct the middle fracture map from rational dimensions and independently chosen basis elements. -> Dimension agreement does not provide the required overlap homotopy or ensure compatible normalization of determinant products.
- **anti-use-unrestricted-union-cochains**: Replace the prescribed filtered cochain complex by all continuous maps into a metrically topologized union. -> This changes the coefficient convention and can lose the common finite stage or pole bound required by ordinary residue tests.
- **anti-use-central-norm-averaging**: Substitute central tame units for the full residual norm quotient in the coheight-one argument. -> Restriction to the center can make a relevant norm character trivial, invalidating the vanishing argument.
- **anti-use-rational-boundary-detection**: Infer that spectral attachments vanish because their rationalizations vanish. -> Rationalization loses attachment information: the paper proves vanishing of every rationalized boundary while establishing a nonzero spectral attachment.

### Panel 3 - reference implementation and oracle

Applicability: `not_applicable`. The finite fracture construction is a categorical construction of spectra from supplied maps and coherent homotopies, rather than a finite computational problem with encoded inputs and decidable output equality. The source states: “Its inputs are a height-two equivalence, a compatible height-one and rational pair of maps, and a basis for the final rational quotient.” The source further states: “The construction produces the stages themselves and computes every connecting map.” These statements occur under sec:fracture; they do not supply a finite executable representation of the required spectra, maps, or homotopies. Checking a finite algebraic surrogate would not decide the asserted spectral equivalences or attachment nonvanishing.

<a id="pm-s5"></a>
## 5. Domain engineering contracts

## 6. Applicability limits and search

- **limit-prime-and-height-regime** (hypothesis): The explicit ordered local-sphere filtration is established for the height-three overlap in the stated prime range. It does not establish the same ordered layers at other heights or excluded primes. Blocked use: ['Applying the explicit filtration outside its prime range.', 'Transplanting its ordered cofibers to a different chromatic height.']
- **limit-localized-fracture-inputs** (hypothesis): The abstract assembly requires the initial localized equivalence, compatible middle maps with a specified homotopy, and an equivalence onto the final rational quotient. Blocked use: ['Constructing the filtration from the cofiber list alone.', 'Applying fracture when the initial map is not the required localized equivalence.', 'Using a final quotient map without proving it is an equivalence.']
- **limit-coherent-choice-dependence** (formal_scope): The attachment identification belongs to the specified realization and its coherent choices. It does not establish uniqueness of the filtration or canonical attachments independent of those choices. Blocked use: ['Comparing attachment formulas after silently changing compatibility homotopies.', 'Claiming all stages and connecting maps are canonical.']
- **limit-cofiber-rotation-sign** (formal_scope): The localization-boundary formula uses the chosen inverse homotopies and the fixed cofiber-rotation convention. Its sign cannot be transferred unchanged to an independently chosen convention. - **limit-filtration-not-wedge** (formal_scope): The constructed filtration does not assert a strong wedge decomposition or a splitting of its first unit. Its first height-one attachment is nonzero for the common realization. Blocked use: ['Replacing the constructed stages by a wedge of their cofibers.', 'Inferring a retraction of the canonical unit from the layer list.']
- **limit-product-compatible-rational-gluing** (hypothesis): Middle gluing requires compatibility of the actual localized maps and the same normalization on the determinant product. Rational dimensions and independent choices of basis elements do not provide this homotopy. Blocked use: ['Gluing the middle block using only rational dimension agreement.', 'Choosing unrelated normalizations for a primitive and its determinant product.']
- **limit-common-algebraic-stage** (formal_scope): Filtered coefficient cochains are formed at the level of complexes and retain a common finite stage or pole bound. They cannot be replaced by all metric-continuous maps into a topologized union. Blocked use: ['Allowing the marking stage to vary without a common bound across a compact cochain domain.', 'Replacing the bounded-pole complex by an unrestricted continuous-map complex.']
- **limit-analytic-versus-integral-sheaf** (formal_scope): The geometric acyclicity concerns the analytic tilted structure sheaf. An integral almost-vanishing assertion cannot be substituted for ordinary vanishing. Blocked use: ['Applying analytic affinoid acyclicity directly to an integral valuation lattice.', 'Discarding an integral almost-zero error without the separate argument controlling it.']
- **limit-annulus-gap-and-banach-tower** (hypothesis): The Kummer contraction requires the stated inner and outer radius gaps. The analytic inverse-limit result requires complete Banach spaces with dense contractive transition maps. Blocked use: ['Using the bounded contracting homotopy on annuli without the required radius gaps.', 'Concluding higher inverse-limit vanishing from density without the completeness and transition-norm hypotheses.']
- **limit-relative-parameter-finiteness** (formal_scope): Finite-dimensionality is a point-valued assertion. With an infinite profinite parameter space, the answer is a continuous-function module and need not remain finite-dimensional over the constant field. Blocked use: ['Reporting parameterized cohomology as finite-dimensional merely because its point-valued fiber is finite-dimensional.']
- **limit-completed-coheight-row** (formal_scope): The completed coheight-one calculation retains a nonconstant orientation row and its residual norm character. A constants-only conclusion requires the subsequent quotient and decompletion arguments. Blocked use: ['Treating the completed norm-kernel calculation as a constants equivalence before taking the required residual invariants.', 'Discarding the extra row without tracking its character.']
- **limit-full-norm-not-center** (edge_case): The coheight-one vanishing argument uses the full residual norm quotient. Replacing it by central tame units can make the relevant character trivial at the exceptional prime discussed in the proof. Blocked use: ['Substituting averaging over the center for invariants of the full norm quotient.', 'Assuming a subgroup section is needed to define the residual quotient action.']
- **limit-finite-resolution-coefficient-topology** (hypothesis): The finite-resolution comparison requires complete linearly topologized coefficients with invariant neighborhoods. Compactness is a separate hypothesis for the asserted compact Hausdorff cohomology and compact/discrete duality. Blocked use: ['Applying compact-coefficient duality directly to an unrestricted algebraic union.', 'Using a finite completed resolution on a coefficient topology without checking invariant neighborhoods.']
- **limit-good-stage-and-framed-line** (hypothesis): Uncompleted finite-stage finiteness is proved at good stages, for stable order lattices, and for coefficient lines with an invariant frame at a finite separable stage. Blocked use: ['Extending finite-stage finiteness to arbitrary coefficient lines without a finite-stage invariant frame.', 'Using an order lattice without verifying stability under the group action.']
- **limit-distinct-frobenius-operators** (formal_scope): Base-field Frobenius fixes variables, whereas coefficient Frobenius on the perfected ring also acts on variable expressions. The coheight-one Cartier operator and the ordinary root projection satisfy different identities and cannot be interchanged. Blocked use: ['Replacing base-field Frobenius descent by Frobenius on all perfected coordinates.', 'Using the ordinary root-projection identity for the coheight-one Cartier operator.']
- **limit-exact-tests-after-completed-terms** (formal_scope): Exact ordinary tests are applied after the completed relative Morava cooperation terms have been formed. The proof does not replace the local completed tensor product by an ordinary tensor product before forming those terms. Blocked use: ['Interchanging ordinary and completed tensor products in the construction of the Amitsur terms.', 'Claiming preservation of an arbitrary totalization without the descendability and error-tower argument.']
- **limit-ordinary-comparison-dependency-order** (formal_scope): The ordinary comparison relies on separately established lattice finiteness, intermediate chromatic finiteness, and bounded-pole finiteness. The result gives convergence in the defining norms without a general finite stopping rule. Blocked use: ['Applying the contraction uniformly to an arbitrary noncompact coefficient family.', 'Treating the qualitative convergence theorem as a certified finite truncation procedure.']
- **limit-witt-tower-transitions** (formal_scope): The finite ghost comparisons do not identify the full uncompleted Witt tower with the ordinary coefficient tower. The reduction transition includes Frobenius, and the argument uses the relevant Frobenius-fixed constant classes. Blocked use: ['Taking an inverse limit of the finite ghost maps as though their transitions were ordinary Witt truncations.', 'Treating the ghost map as the identity on all finite-field Witt constants.']
- **limit-derived-completion-before-rationalization** (nonconstructive): The integral orientation is obtained through compatible finite-length classes and a derived coefficient limit. This does not supply a finite computational encoding of the resulting spectral map, and rationalization cannot replace the prescribed integral limit argument. - **limit-rational-scalar-not-integral-unit** (formal_scope): The compatibility normalization rescales the rational source by a nonzero rational scalar. Blocked use: ['Strengthening the nonzero rational scalar comparison to an integral-unit comparison.', 'Changing the integral orientation generator to implement the rational normalization.']

- **limit-rationalization-loses-attachments** (formal_scope): Vanishing of the rationalized connecting maps does not establish nullity of the underlying spectral attachments. Blocked use: ['Using rationalized boundary vanishing as a splitting test for the original filtration.']
- **limit-geometric-solid-action** (hypothesis): The solid finite-resolution argument requires an actual continuous action on the derived condensed coefficient object. An action on point-valued cohomology alone is insufficient. Blocked use: ['Inferring a condensed equivariant comparison solely from its point-valued representation.', 'Applying scalar row actions without retaining the geometric group parameters.']
- **limit-infinite-building-versus-finite-computation** (formal_scope): Local finiteness and a chamber fundamental domain do not make the entire reduced building a finite complex.           "exact_quote": "Let $F$ be a non-Archimedean local field with normalized valuation $\\nu$, valuation ring $\\mathcal O$, uniformizer $\\pi$, and residue field $\\kappa$ of cardinality $q$. Let $\\mathcal B$ be the reduced affine building of $\\mathrm{GL}_3(F)$, equivalently the building of $\\mathrm{PGL}_3(F)$, and put $$J_3(F)=\\{g\\in\\mathrm{GL}_3(F):\\nu(\\det g)=0\\}.$$ Then $\\mathcal B$ is a contractible, locally finite, two-dimensional simplicial complex. Each vertex has $2(q^2+q+1)$ adjacent vertices. The group $J_3(F)$ preserves vertex types. The setwise stabilizer of every nonempty face is compact open in $J_3(F)$ and fixes that face pointwise. Any closed chamber is a fundamental domain, including all its faces.",
          "source_id": "PM-318.2"

<a id="pm-s7"></a>
## 7. Complete mathematical paper


For every prime <i>p</i> ≥ 5, we construct an explicit eight-stage filtration of $`L_2L_{K(3)}\mathbb S_p^\wedge`$ by the local-sphere layers in the height-three chromatic-splitting pattern. The map from its first stage to the overlap is the canonical unit, and two signed fracture formulas identify all attachments for the chosen local maps and compatibility homotopy. A companion canonical-map theorem further implies that the first height-one attachment is nonzero.

<a id="sec:introduction"></a>
### Introduction

Fix a prime $p$. Write $L_i=L_{E(i)}$ for localization at Johnson–Wilson theory and $L_{K(i)}$ for localization at Morava $K$-theory. We use the derived $p$-completion $S=\mathbb S_p^\wedge$ of the sphere and study the overlap $$T=L_{K(3)}S,\qquad X=L_2T.$$ The object $X$ is the part of the height-three local sphere visible below height three. Our question is how to build it from lower local spheres while retaining the maps by which the pieces are joined.

Chromatic fracture makes the gluing problem precise. An $E(2)$-local spectrum is a homotopy pullback of its $K(2)$-local and $E(1)$-local parts over their common localization. The gluing map is part of the data; the fracture square does not determine it from the two corners alone (Barthel and Beaudry 2020, sec. 2.4, diagram (2.19)) <a id="pm-cite-1"></a>[[BB](#ref-BB)]. Hopkins’ chromatic splitting conjecture, as recorded by Hovey (Hovey 1995, Conjecture 4.2) <a id="pm-cite-2"></a>[[Hovey](#ref-Hovey)], proposes classes, factorizations, and summands that would split the relevant canonical cofiber sequence. The revised strong formulation of Barthel–Beaudry (Barthel and Beaudry 2020, Conjecture 6.3 and Remark 6.4) <a id="pm-cite-3"></a>[[BB](#ref-BB)] has the same lower-sphere pattern at the height and primes considered here. We study an ordered filtration with those cofibers and a canonical first unit, allowing nonzero connecting maps.

The low-height results already distinguish these formulations. Hovey’s July 1993 account records the height-one case and the height-two case at primes greater than three, attributing the latter to Hopkins using Shimomura–Yabe (Hovey 1995, 17–19) <a id="pm-cite-4"></a>[[Hovey](#ref-Hovey)]. Goerss–Henn–Mahowald later proved the height-two splitting at the prime three (Goerss, Henn, and Mahowald 2014, Theorem 1.2) <a id="pm-cite-5"></a>[[GoerssHennMahowald2014](#ref-GoerssHennMahowald2014)]. Their proof identifies the actual rational comparison map before applying chromatic fracture (Goerss, Henn, and Mahowald 2014, proof of Theorem 5.11, p. 1288) <a id="pm-cite-6"></a>[[GoerssHennMahowald2014](#ref-GoerssHennMahowald2014)]. At height two and the prime two, Beaudry disproved the original strong form (Beaudry 2017, Theorem 1.4) <a id="pm-cite-7"></a>[[Beaudry2017](#ref-Beaudry2017)]; Beaudry–Goerss–Henn established a corrected decomposition with Moore-spectrum terms that retains the weak unit splitting (Beaudry, Goerss, and Henn 2022, Theorem 1.1.6) <a id="pm-cite-8"></a>[[BGH2022](#ref-BGH2022)].

Two established calculations explain the pieces at height three. At odd primes the height-two splitting gives two $E(1)$-local pieces and two rational pieces (Barthel and Beaudry 2020, Theorem 6.7) <a id="pm-cite-9"></a>[[BB](#ref-BB)]. At every prime and positive height, the theorem of Barthel–Schlank–Stapleton–Weinstein computes the rational homotopy of the $K(n)$-local sphere as an exterior algebra over $\mathbb Q_p$ on generators of degrees $1-2i$, $1\leq i\leq n$ (Barthel et al. 2025, Theorem A). At height three the resulting degrees are $$0,\ -1,\ -3,\ -4,\ -5,\ -6,\ -8,\ -9.$$ This algebra calculation determines neither integral representatives nor their images under lower-height localization. Those map identifications are what allow the layers to be assembled.

<a id="pm-h-3"></a>
#### The explicit filtration

All spectra and maps in the theorem carry their natural $S$-module structures. A filtration means a sequence of homotopy cofiber sequences: its $i$-th cofiber $C_i$ has a connecting map $\partial_i:C_i\to\Sigma F_{i-1}$.

<a id="stmt-thm-main"></a>
<div id="thm:main" class="theorem">

**Theorem 1** (Explicit height-three filtration). *For every prime $p\geq5$, there are $E(2)$-local $S$-modules and maps $$0=F_0\longrightarrow F_1\longrightarrow\cdots\longrightarrow F_8,
 \qquad e:F_8\xrightarrow{\simeq}X,$$ whose successive cofibers $C_i=\mathop{\mathrm{cofib}}(F_{i-1}\to F_i)$, in order, are $$\begin{array}{c|l@{\qquad\qquad}c|l}
i&C_i&i&C_i\\ \hline
1&L_2S&5&\Sigma^{-5}H\mathbb Q_p\\
2&\Sigma^{-1}L_2S&6&\Sigma^{-6}H\mathbb Q_p\\
3&\Sigma^{-3}L_1S&7&\Sigma^{-8}H\mathbb Q_p\\
4&\Sigma^{-4}L_1S&8&\Sigma^{-9}H\mathbb Q_p.
\end{array}$$ Under $F_1\simeq L_2S$, the composite $F_1\to F_8\xrightarrow e X$ is the canonical map $L_2(S\to L_{K(3)}S)$.*

</div>

The attachment identification is a separate formal part of the result. Once the stages and their fracture data have been defined, [thm:attachment-identification](#thm:attachment-identification) collects every connecting map and both signed roofs. The application in [sec:application](#sec:application) establishes [thm:main](#thm:main) and the height-three instance of [thm:attachment-identification](#thm:attachment-identification) from one choice of local maps, compatibility homotopy, and coherent inverse data. The first unit is canonical; the attachment identification is relative to those choices.

Existence of a canonical-unit filtration with these cofibers is also the height-three case of (OpenAI 2026b, Theorem 1.1) <a id="pm-cite-10"></a>[[CompanionFilteredChromaticSplitting](#ref-CompanionFilteredChromaticSplitting)], whose range $p>n+1$ becomes $p\geq5$ here. That theorem supplies one family of product bases at all lower positive heights. The present proof constructs the height-three maps independently of that theorem, identifies the rational degree-three comparison, and records every attachment relative to one compatible set of choices. Neither filtration statement asserts the strong wedge or splits its first unit. The construction of [thm:main](#thm:main) is independent of the rational-obstruction theorem used in [sec:attachment](#sec:attachment). That separate theorem supplies additional information about the extensions: for this explicit filtration, the first height-one connecting map is nonzero.

<a id="pm-h-4"></a>
#### Three blocks and two gluing problems

Put $Q=L_0S\simeq H\mathbb Q_p$, and group the layers as $$\begin{aligned}
 W&=L_2S\vee\Sigma^{-1}L_2S,\\
 U_{\mathrm{mid}}&=\Sigma^{-3}L_1S\vee\Sigma^{-4}L_1S,\\
 V&=\Sigma^{-5}Q\vee\Sigma^{-6}Q
       \vee\Sigma^{-8}Q\vee\Sigma^{-9}Q.
\end{aligned}$$ The first localized basis is an actual map $$w=(1,\zeta):W\longrightarrow X,$$ where $\zeta:\Sigma^{-1}S\to T$ is the integral determinant class. It becomes an equivalence after $K(2)$-localization. Hence its cofiber $Y$ is $E(1)$-local. To insert the two summands of $U_{\mathrm{mid}}$, one needs a map to $Y$, not merely the knowledge that $Y$ has the expected local homotopy groups.

There are two descriptions of that map. At height one, an integral orientation class $\delta\in\pi_{-3}L_{K(1)}T$ participates in the actual basis $$(1,\zeta,\delta,\zeta\delta):
 R_1\vee\Sigma^{-1}R_1\vee\Sigma^{-3}R_1\vee\Sigma^{-4}R_1
 \xrightarrow{\simeq}L_{K(1)}T,\qquad R_1=L_{K(1)}S.$$ The first two components are localizations of the same maps used in $w$; quotienting them gives the $K(1)$-local part of a map from $U_{\mathrm{mid}}$. Rationally, the degree-three primitive $\alpha_3\in\pi_{-3}L_0T$ maps to $c\delta$ for a nonzero $c\in\mathbb Q_p$, and its product with $\zeta$ maps to $c\zeta\delta$. Rescaling only the rational primitive by $c^{-1}$ makes the two descriptions agree on the rationalized $K(1)$-local overlap. The height-one fracture square then constructs $$h:U_{\mathrm{mid}}\longrightarrow Y.$$ The specified compatibility homotopy, rather than a dimension count, is the input to this gluing step.

Pulling $X\to Y$ back along the first summand and then all of $U_{\mathrm{mid}}$ gives $F_3$ and $F_4$. The cofiber of $F_4\to X$ is rational. The four remaining exterior products give an actual equivalence from $V$ to that cofiber, and their ordered partial sums give $F_5,\ldots,F_8$ by pullback. The terminal projection is an equivalence because the full map from $V$ is. The proof in [sec:fracture](#sec:fracture) follows the two fracture squares far enough to identify their connecting maps, including both rotation signs.

<a id="pm-h-5"></a>
#### Why the localized bases require geometry

The two coefficient comparisons use the loci of the height-three deformation where the connected part has height two and height one. Their étale parts have heights one and two, respectively; these are the coheight-one and ordinary strata. Finite marking towers on these loci are related to extensions of vector bundles on the Fargues–Fontaine curve. The bundle and local-system framework comes from Fargues–Fontaine and Scholze–Weinstein (Fargues and Fontaine 2018; Scholze and Weinstein 2013) <a id="pm-cite-11"></a>[[FarguesFontaine](#ref-FarguesFontaine), [ScholzeWeinstein](#ref-ScholzeWeinstein)]; relative full faithfulness of derived sections is supplied by Anschütz–Le Bras (Anschütz and Le Bras 2025, Corollary 3.11) <a id="pm-cite-12"></a>[[AnschuetzLeBrasFourier](#ref-AnschuetzLeBrasFourier)]. Retaining the integral Tate frames and the determinant lattice makes the group actions and the determinant product identity part of the comparison. These data are later used to identify the coefficient classes of the unit and determinant maps in $w=(1,\zeta)$.

The Kummer and translation calculations in the coheight-one work of Barthel–Mann–Ray–Schlank–Senger–Weinstein–Zhou (Barthel et al. 2026, secs. 3.3–3.6) <a id="pm-cite-13"></a>[[BMR](#ref-BMR)] provide methodological context for the cohomology of the completed strata. The geometric answers must then be carried to the algebraic coefficients in ordinary Morava cooperations. A cochain in their marking union must occur at one finite stage on its compact domain; a cochain with Laurent coefficients must have one pole bound. Completion does not preserve those requirements by definition, so the comparisons must establish the required finite bounds before returning to the algebraic coefficients.

On the locus with connected height two, the completed calculation controls cohomology at each finite stage of the connected marking tower. The comparison in [h3:sec:coheight-one](#h3:sec:coheight-one) proves finite cohomology for a cofinal family of finite products of complete local fields, then removes completion while preserving the group actions and the constants map. The descent calculation in [h3:sec:descent](#h3:sec:descent) then uses these algebraic coefficients to prove that the actual unit and determinant map $w=(1,\zeta)$ is a $K(2)$-equivalence.

On the locus with connected height one, the completed calculation provides the constants comparison determined by the Tate frame of rank two and the connected part. To reach the ordinary coefficients, [h3:sec:ordinary](#h3:sec:ordinary) first proves finite cohomology for each compact lattice of power series. An intermediate chromatic descent calculation then supplies finite cohomology for the union of coefficients with bounded poles. Only after this step is the analytic completion removed. The resulting constants comparison is the input to [h3:sec:integral-basis](#h3:sec:integral-basis), where finite Witt coefficients carry the orientation through compatible length transitions and derived completion produces $\delta$.

The rational comparison uses these integral maps and the established rational exterior algebra, whose height-three proof is reconstructed in [h3:app:rational-boundary](#h3:app:rational-boundary) following (Barthel et al. 2025) <a id="pm-cite-14"></a>[[BSSW](#ref-BSSW)]. transports a trace class in degree three along the actual Tate frame of rank two on the ordinary stratum. The finite Witt comparisons carry this class through the coefficient tower, whose derived limit is taken before rationalization. The resulting comparison proves that its image in the line $\mathbb Q_p\delta$ is nonzero. This supplies the scalar $c$ in the gluing overview. Product naturality for the same $\zeta$ gives the same scalar on $\zeta\alpha_3$.

<a id="pm-h-6"></a>
#### Reading the proof

first constructs the ordered filtration from precisely stated local maps and a compatibility homotopy, and identifies all its attachments for those same choices. The remainder of the paper constructs the required maps.

fixes the coefficient, group, and cochain conventions. [h3:sec:towers](#h3:sec:towers) constructs the finite Tate-coordinate towers and their integral frame comparisons, and [h3:sec:analytic](#h3:sec:analytic) computes the completed strata with their actual constants maps. [h3:sec:coheight-one](#h3:sec:coheight-one) removes completion on the coheight-one stratum, using finite local-field stages and the full reduced-norm quotient. [h3:sec:descent](#h3:sec:descent) then compares ordinary residue cooperations with those stages and obtains the actual height-two basis.

proves the second coefficient comparison in the order required by its dependencies: root and Laurent-tail control, compact lattice finiteness, intermediate chromatic finiteness, bounded-pole finiteness, and only then the natural ordinary comparison. [h3:sec:integral-basis](#h3:sec:integral-basis) carries the orientation through finite Witt coefficients and derived completion to the actual height-one basis. The trace argument of [h3:sec:rational](#h3:sec:rational) identifies the localization of the particular degree-three primitive.

Finally, [sec:application](#sec:application) inserts these maps into the earlier fracture construction, proving the main theorem and its attachment identification from one common choice. [sec:attachment](#sec:attachment) proves a conditional criterion for the first middle attachment and applies the companion canonical-map theorem through the local completion, localization, and scalar comparisons proved there. [h3:app:rational-boundary](#h3:app:rational-boundary) then reconstructs the rational exterior algebra from its arithmetic and geometric inputs.

<a id="sec:fracture"></a>
### A finite fracture construction

This section isolates the topological assembly. Its inputs are a height-two equivalence, a compatible height-one and rational pair of maps, and a basis for the final rational quotient. The construction produces the stages themselves and computes every connecting map. It does not use the coefficient calculations of [h3:sec:ordinary](#h3:sec:ordinary).

<a id="pm-h-8"></a>
#### Module localizations and rotation signs

<a id="eq:module-localization"></a>
Put $Q=L_0S\simeq H\mathbb Q_p$ and $J=K(1)\vee K(2)$. We work in $\mathop{\mathrm{Mod}}_S$. Homological Bousfield localization $L_E$ lifts to this category with the same underlying spectrum, whether or not it is smashing. Indeed, $S^{\wedge n}\wedge M\to S^{\wedge n}\wedge L_EM$ is an $E$-equivalence for every $n$. Mapping into the local spectrum $L_EM$ extends the action maps and their coherent unit and associativity homotopies. The free-module bar resolution then gives, for every local $S$-module $N$, $$\label{eq:module-localization}
 \mathop{\mathrm{Map}}_{\mathop{\mathrm{Mod}}_S}(L_EM,N)\simeq\mathop{\mathrm{Map}}_{\mathop{\mathrm{Mod}}_S}(M,N).$$ Thus the units below are module maps. The forgetful functor creates limits and detects equivalences, so the spectral fracture pullbacks are also pullbacks of $S$-modules.

<a id="eq:rational-adjunction"></a>
Rationalization is extension of scalars: $Q\otimes_SM\simeq L_0M$. In particular, for a rational module $D$, $$\label{eq:rational-adjunction}
 \mathop{\mathrm{Map}}_{\mathop{\mathrm{Mod}}_S}(M,D)
   \simeq\mathop{\mathrm{Map}}_{\mathop{\mathrm{Mod}}_Q}(L_0M,D).$$ A map from a finite sum of shifts of $Q$ is determined up to homotopy by the images of its module generators. A homotopy between the rational maps in <a href="#eq:rational-adjunction" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:rational-adjunction">[eq:rational-adjunction]</a> gives the corresponding $S$-module homotopy after precomposition by $M\to L_0M$.

<a id="eq:height-two-fracture"></a>
<a id="eq:positive-fracture"></a>
The height-two fracture square for an $E(2)$-local module $B$ is $$\label{eq:height-two-fracture}
 B\simeq L_{K(2)}B
       \mathbin{\times}_{L_1L_{K(2)}B}L_1B.$$ For an $E(1)$-local module the corresponding square uses $K(1)$ and $L_0$ (Barthel and Beaudry 2020, sec. 2.4, diagram (2.19)) <a id="pm-cite-15"></a>[[BB](#ref-BB)]. Consequently an $E(2)$-local, $K(2)$-acyclic module is $E(1)$-local, and an $E(2)$-local module acyclic for both $K(1)$ and $K(2)$ is rational. There is also a fracture square separating all positive heights: $$\label{eq:positive-fracture}
 B\simeq L_JB\mathbin{\times}_{L_0L_JB}L_0B.$$ To see this, $L_JB$ is $E(2)$-local because $\langle E(2)\rangle=\langle K(0)\vee J\rangle$. The fiber $N=\mathop{\mathrm{fib}}(B\to L_JB)$ is therefore $E(2)$-local and $J$-acyclic, hence rational. Exactness of $L_0$ identifies it with $\mathop{\mathrm{fib}}(L_0B\to L_0L_JB)$, which proves <a href="#eq:positive-fracture" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:positive-fracture">[eq:positive-fracture]</a>.

For $f:A\to B$ and $C=\mathop{\mathrm{cofib}}(f)$, we fix the cofiber-rotation convention $$A\xrightarrow{f}B\longrightarrow C\longrightarrow\Sigma A
 \xrightarrow{-\Sigma f}\Sigma B.$$ If $i:N\to A$ is the fiber of $A\to D$, the induced identification $\mathop{\mathrm{cofib}}(A\to D)\simeq\Sigma N$ therefore makes the boundary to $\Sigma A$ equal to $-\Sigma i$.

<a id="stmt-lem-boundary"></a>
<div id="lem:boundary" class="lemma">

<a id="eq:boundary-lemma"></a>
**Lemma 2** (Boundary of a localization comparison). *Let $a:A\to B$ be a map in a stable category, and let $L$ be an exact localization for which $La$ is an equivalence. Choose an inverse of $La$ and its inverse homotopies, and put $$\tau:B\longrightarrow LB\xrightarrow{(La)^{-1}}LA,\qquad
 N=\mathop{\mathrm{fib}}(A\longrightarrow LA).$$ The inverse homotopy makes $\tau$ a map under $A$, and therefore gives $$\bar\tau:\mathop{\mathrm{cofib}}(a)\longrightarrow\mathop{\mathrm{cofib}}(A\to LA)
                         \simeq\Sigma N.$$ If $i:N\to A$ is the fiber inclusion, then the connecting map of the cofiber sequence of $a$ is $$\label{eq:boundary-lemma}
 \partial_a=(-\Sigma i)\bar\tau.$$ If $M$ is another exact localization and $N$ is $M$-local, the middle cofiber can equivalently be written $\mathop{\mathrm{cofib}}(MA\to MLA)$, using its localization identification.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-lem-boundary"><summary>Proof of stmt-lem-boundary</summary>

*Proof.* The under-$A$ homotopy supplies a map of cofiber sequences $$\begin{tikzcd}[column sep=large]
A \arrow[r,"a"] \arrow[d,equal]
  & B \arrow[r] \arrow[d,"\tau"]
  & \mathop{\mathrm{cofib}}(a) \arrow[r,"\partial_a"] \arrow[d,"\bar\tau"]
  & \Sigma A \arrow[d,equal]\\
A \arrow[r]
  & LA \arrow[r]
  & \Sigma N \arrow[r,"-\Sigma i"]
  & \Sigma A.
\end{tikzcd}$$ The right square is <a href="#eq:boundary-lemma" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:boundary-lemma">[eq:boundary-lemma]</a>; its sign is the rotation sign fixed above. If $N$ is $M$-local, so is $\mathop{\mathrm{cofib}}(A\to LA)\simeq\Sigma N$. Its $M$-localization map is then an equivalence, and exactness identifies the localized cofiber with $\mathop{\mathrm{cofib}}(MA\to MLA)$. ◻

</details>

<a id="pm-h-9"></a>
#### The stages and their boundaries

Use the following ordered blocks: $$\begin{aligned}
 W&=W_1\vee W_2=L_2S\vee\Sigma^{-1}L_2S,\\
 U_{\mathrm{mid}}&=U_3\vee U_4=\Sigma^{-3}L_1S\vee\Sigma^{-4}L_1S,\\
 V&=V_5\vee V_6\vee V_7\vee V_8\\
  &=\Sigma^{-5}Q\vee\Sigma^{-6}Q
       \vee\Sigma^{-8}Q\vee\Sigma^{-9}Q.
\end{aligned}$$

<a id="stmt-prop-fracture"></a>
<div id="prop:fracture" class="proposition">

**Proposition 3** (Ordered fracture filtration). *Let $X$ be an $E(2)$-local $S$-module. Suppose the following module maps and homotopies are given.*

1.  *A map $w:W\to X$ for which $L_{K(2)}w$ is an equivalence. Put $Y=\mathop{\mathrm{cofib}}(w)$, with quotient $q:X\to Y$.*

<a id="eq:compatibility"></a>
2.  *An equivalence $\kappa:L_{K(1)}U_{\mathrm{mid}}\xrightarrow{\simeq}L_{K(1)}Y$, a rational map $r:L_0U_{\mathrm{mid}}\to L_0Y$, and a specified homotopy of $Q$-module maps between $$\label{eq:compatibility}
      \begin{gathered}
      L_0U_{\mathrm{mid}}\longrightarrow L_0L_{K(1)}U_{\mathrm{mid}}
              \xrightarrow{L_0\kappa}L_0L_{K(1)}Y,\\
      L_0U_{\mathrm{mid}}\xrightarrow rL_0Y\longrightarrow L_0L_{K(1)}Y.
      \end{gathered}$$*

<a id="eq:quotient-basis"></a>
3.  *A map $b:V\to L_0X$ for which $$\label{eq:quotient-basis}
      t_0:V\xrightarrow bL_0X\xrightarrow{L_0q}L_0Y
                     \longrightarrow\mathop{\mathrm{cofib}}(r)$$ is an equivalence.*

*Then there is a filtration in $E(2)$-local $S$-modules $$0=F_0\longrightarrow F_1\longrightarrow\cdots\longrightarrow F_8
 \xrightarrow[\simeq]{e}X$$ with ordered cofibers $W_1,W_2,U_3,U_4,V_5,V_6,V_7,V_8$. The composite $F_2=W\to F_8\xrightarrow eX$ is $w$.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-prop-fracture"><summary>Proof of stmt-prop-fracture</summary>

<a id="eq:middle-map"></a>
*Proof.* *Constructing the middle map.* The cofiber $Y$ is $E(2)$-local and $K(2)$-acyclic by <span class="upright">(i)</span>, hence $E(1)$-local. Exactness identifies it naturally with $\mathop{\mathrm{cofib}}(L_1w)$. Its height-one fracture square is $$Y\simeq L_{K(1)}Y\mathbin{\times}_{L_0L_{K(1)}Y}L_0Y.$$ The two proposed maps from $U_{\mathrm{mid}}$ to its corners are $$U_{\mathrm{mid}}\longrightarrow L_{K(1)}U_{\mathrm{mid}}\xrightarrow{\kappa}L_{K(1)}Y,
 \qquad
 U_{\mathrm{mid}}\longrightarrow L_0U_{\mathrm{mid}}\xrightarrow rL_0Y.$$ By <a href="#eq:rational-adjunction" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:rational-adjunction">[eq:rational-adjunction]</a>, the specified rational homotopy in <a href="#eq:compatibility" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:compatibility">[eq:compatibility]</a> identifies their composites to the overlap as $S$-module maps. The pullback therefore gives $$\label{eq:middle-map}
 h:U_{\mathrm{mid}}\longrightarrow Y,\qquad L_{K(1)}h=\kappa,\quad L_0h=r.$$ Here each equality includes the homotopy obtained from the corresponding pullback projection: localizing that homotopy and using idempotence gives the displayed identification. In particular, $h$ is a $K(1)$-equivalence.

<a id="eq:first-boundaries"></a>
*The first four stages.* Let $\partial_w:Y\to\Sigma W$ be the boundary of $w$, and put $$d=\partial_wh:U_{\mathrm{mid}}\longrightarrow\Sigma W,\qquad
 d_i=d|_{U_i}\quad(i=3,4).$$ Define <a id="eq:first-stages"></a>$$\label{eq:first-stages}
 F_0=0,\quad F_1=W_1,\quad F_2=W,\quad
 F_3=X\mathbin{\times}_YU_3,\quad
 F_4=X\mathbin{\times}_YU_{\mathrm{mid}}.$$ The first nonzero transition is the wedge inclusion $W_1\to W$. The identification $X\times_Y0\simeq W$ makes the next transitions the pullbacks of $0\to U_3\to U_3\vee U_4$. In a stable category a pullback square is also a pushout square. Their cofibers are consequently $U_3$ and $U_4$, and $$F_3\simeq\mathop{\mathrm{fib}}(d_3:U_3\to\Sigma W),\qquad
 F_4\simeq\mathop{\mathrm{fib}}(d:U_{\mathrm{mid}}\to\Sigma W).$$ Naturality of the cofiber sequence for each pullback gives $$\label{eq:first-boundaries}
 \partial_1=0,\qquad \partial_2=0,\qquad
 \partial_3=d_3,\qquad
 \partial_4=\Sigma(F_2\to F_3)d_4.$$ For the last formula, the quotient of the pullback square for $U_3\to U_3\vee U_4$ identifies its quotient with $U_4$. There is a map of cofiber sequences from $W\to F_4\to U_{\mathrm{mid}}$ to $F_3\to F_4\to U_4$, whose components are $W\to F_3$, the identity of $F_4$, and the projection $\operatorname{pr}_4:U_{\mathrm{mid}}\to U_4$. Its boundary square gives $\partial_4\operatorname{pr}_4=\Sigma(W\to F_3)d$. Restricting to the summand $U_4$ gives the displayed formula.

<a id="eq:first-roof"></a>
We next express $d$ through the height-two fracture map. Choose coherent inverse data for $L_{K(2)}w$, and form $$\tau_2:L_1X\longrightarrow L_1L_{K(2)}X
       \xrightarrow{(L_1L_{K(2)}w)^{-1}}L_1L_{K(2)}W.$$ It is a map under $L_1W$, so it induces $$\bar\tau_2:Y\simeq\mathop{\mathrm{cofib}}(L_1w)
       \longrightarrow\mathop{\mathrm{cofib}}(L_1W\to L_1L_{K(2)}W).$$ Let $j_W:\mathop{\mathrm{fib}}(W\to L_{K(2)}W)\to W$ be the fiber inclusion. Then $$\label{eq:first-roof}
\begin{split}
 d:\ U_{\mathrm{mid}}\xrightarrow hY\xrightarrow{\bar\tau_2}
 &\mathop{\mathrm{cofib}}(L_1W\longrightarrow L_1L_{K(2)}W)\\
 &\simeq\Sigma\mathop{\mathrm{fib}}(W\longrightarrow L_{K(2)}W)
   \xrightarrow{-\Sigma j_W}\Sigma W.
\end{split}$$ Indeed, <a href="#eq:height-two-fracture" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:height-two-fracture">[eq:height-two-fracture]</a> identifies the fiber of $W\to L_{K(2)}W$ with the fiber of $L_1W\to L_1L_{K(2)}W$; it is $E(1)$-local. [lem:boundary](#lem:boundary), with $L=L_{K(2)}$ and $M=L_1$, then says that the composite from $Y$ in <a href="#eq:first-roof" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:first-roof">[eq:first-roof]</a> is exactly $\partial_w$. This proves the formula and fixes its minus sign.

<a id="eq:quotient-identification"></a>
*The rational quotient.* Let $a:F_4\to X$ be the pullback projection and set $Z=\mathop{\mathrm{cofib}}(a)$. Taking the cofiber of the pullback square defining $F_4$ gives a natural equivalence $$\label{eq:quotient-identification}
 Z\simeq\mathop{\mathrm{cofib}}(h:U_{\mathrm{mid}}\longrightarrow Y).$$ This cofiber is $E(1)$-local and $K(1)$-acyclic by <a href="#eq:middle-map" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:middle-map">[eq:middle-map]</a>, hence rational. Thus $a$ is an equivalence after localization at $K(1)$ or $K(2)$, and therefore after $L_J$. Rationalizing <a href="#eq:quotient-identification" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:quotient-identification">[eq:quotient-identification]</a> identifies $Z\simeq\mathop{\mathrm{cofib}}(r)$.

<a id="eq:terminal-quotient"></a>
Write $z:X\to Z$ for the quotient. Since $Z$ is rational, <a href="#eq:rational-adjunction" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:rational-adjunction">[eq:rational-adjunction]</a> gives its factorization $\widetilde z:L_0X\to Z$. Under the preceding cofiber identification, the map in <span class="upright">(iii)</span> is $$\label{eq:terminal-quotient}
 t=\widetilde z\,b:V\xrightarrow{\simeq}Z.$$ This records the factorization used to compare the last attachments with fracture.

*The last four stages.* Let $V_{\leq j}$ be the first $j$ summands of $V$, for $0\leq j\leq4$, and use the restriction of $t$ to define <a id="eq:last-stages"></a>$$\label{eq:last-stages}
 F_{4+j}=X\mathbin{\times}_ZV_{\leq j}.$$ At $j=0$, the cofiber sequence of $a$ identifies this definition with the previous $F_4$, over $X$. The cofiber of $V_{\leq j-1}\to V_{\leq j}$ is $V_{4+j}$. Exact pullback gives the same cofiber for $F_{4+j-1}\to F_{4+j}$.

<a id="eq:last-boundaries"></a>
Let $\partial_a:Z\to\Sigma F_4$ be the boundary of $a$, put $g=\partial_at$, and write $g_i=g|_{V_i}$. The quotient-of-a-pullback argument used above gives every remaining connecting map: $$\label{eq:last-boundaries}
 \partial_i=\Sigma(F_4\to F_{i-1})g_i:
 V_i\longrightarrow\Sigma F_{i-1},\qquad 5\leq i\leq8.$$

<a id="eq:second-roof"></a>
The map $g$ is described by the positive-height fracture square. Choose coherent inverse data for $L_Ja$, and let $j_a:\mathop{\mathrm{fib}}(F_4\to L_JF_4)\to F_4$ be the fiber inclusion. The formula is $$\label{eq:second-roof}
\begin{aligned}[b]
 g:\ V\xrightarrow bL_0X\longrightarrow L_0L_JX
 &\xrightarrow{(L_0L_Ja)^{-1}}L_0L_JF_4\\
 &\longrightarrow\mathop{\mathrm{cofib}}(L_0F_4\longrightarrow L_0L_JF_4)\\
 &\simeq\Sigma\mathop{\mathrm{fib}}(F_4\longrightarrow L_JF_4)
   \xrightarrow{-\Sigma j_a}\Sigma F_4.
\end{aligned}$$ We verify in particular why this roof begins with $b$, rather than only with the quotient equivalence $t$. Put $$C_a=\mathop{\mathrm{cofib}}(F_4\to L_JF_4),\qquad
 \tau_J=(L_Ja)^{-1}\circ(X\to L_JX),$$ and let $q_a:L_JF_4\to C_a$ be the quotient. The chosen inverse homotopy makes $\tau_Ja$ the localization unit of $F_4$. [lem:boundary](#lem:boundary) gives $\bar\tau_J:Z\to C_a$, with a specified homotopy $$\bar\tau_Jz\simeq q_a\tau_J.$$ Both $Z$ and $C_a$ are rational: for $C_a$ this follows from <a href="#eq:positive-fracture" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:positive-fracture">[eq:positive-fracture]</a>. If $\rho:C_a\xrightarrow{\simeq}L_0C_a$ is its localization map, the rational adjunction transports the last homotopy to $$\rho\bar\tau_J\widetilde z\simeq (L_0q_a)(L_0\tau_J).$$ Using $t=\widetilde z b$, this becomes $$\rho\bar\tau_Jt\simeq
 (L_0q_a)(L_0L_Ja)^{-1}\circ
 (L_0X\to L_0L_JX)\circ b.$$ Exactness identifies $L_0C_a$ with the cofiber in <a href="#eq:second-roof" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:second-roof">[eq:second-roof]</a>. The boundary formula $\partial_a=(-\Sigma j_a)\bar\tau_J$ now identifies that entire roof with $\partial_at=g$, including the second minus sign.

Finally, <a href="#eq:terminal-quotient" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:terminal-quotient">[eq:terminal-quotient]</a> makes the projection $$e:F_8=X\times_ZV\longrightarrow X$$ an equivalence. All stages use finite limits or colimits of $E(2)$-local $S$-modules, so they remain in that category. Their maps to $X$ extend $w$; hence $F_2\to F_8\xrightarrow eX$ is $w$. ◻

</details>

<a id="stmt-thm-attachment-identification"></a>
<div id="thm:attachment-identification" class="theorem">

**Theorem 4** (Attachment identification for the ordered fracture filtration). *Fix the data $w,\kappa,r,b$ and the compatibility homotopy of [prop:fracture](#prop:fracture). Choose coherent inverse data for $L_{K(2)}w$, and carry out that proposition’s construction. Use exactly its fracture map $h$, pullback stages $F_i$, projection $a:F_4\to X$, quotient $Z=\mathop{\mathrm{cofib}}(a)$, equivalence $t=\widetilde z b:V\xrightarrow{\simeq}Z$, and terminal projection $e:F_8\to X$, choosing the coherent inverse data for $L_Ja$ at the indicated step. Under the resulting ordered cofiber identifications $$W_1,\ W_2,\ U_3,\ U_4,\ V_5,\ V_6,\ V_7,\ V_8,$$ the connecting maps of this same filtration are $$\begin{gathered}
 \partial_1=0,\qquad \partial_2=0,\qquad
 \partial_3=d_3,\qquad
 \partial_4=\Sigma(F_2\to F_3)d_4,\\
 \partial_i=\Sigma(F_4\to F_{i-1})g_i
 \qquad(5\leq i\leq8),
\end{gathered}$$ where $d=\partial_wh$, $g=\partial_at$, $d_i=d|_{U_i}$, and $g_i=g|_{V_i}$. The maps $d$ and $g$ are the signed roofs $$\begin{aligned}
 d:\ U_{\mathrm{mid}}\xrightarrow hY\xrightarrow{\bar\tau_2}
 &\mathop{\mathrm{cofib}}(L_1W\longrightarrow L_1L_{K(2)}W)\\
 &\simeq\Sigma\mathop{\mathrm{fib}}(W\longrightarrow L_{K(2)}W)
   \xrightarrow{-\Sigma j_W}\Sigma W,
\end{aligned}$$ and $$\begin{aligned}
 g:\ V\xrightarrow bL_0X\longrightarrow L_0L_JX
 &\xrightarrow{(L_0L_Ja)^{-1}}L_0L_JF_4\\
 &\longrightarrow\mathop{\mathrm{cofib}}(L_0F_4\longrightarrow L_0L_JF_4)\\
 &\simeq\Sigma\mathop{\mathrm{fib}}(F_4\longrightarrow L_JF_4)
   \xrightarrow{-\Sigma j_a}\Sigma F_4.
\end{aligned}$$ Here $\bar\tau_2,j_W,j_a$ are the maps defined from the same construction and inverse data above.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-thm-attachment-identification"><summary>Proof of stmt-thm-attachment-identification</summary>

*Proof.* The proof of [prop:fracture](#prop:fracture) established <a href="#eq:first-boundaries" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:first-boundaries">[eq:first-boundaries]</a> and <a href="#eq:last-boundaries" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:last-boundaries">[eq:last-boundaries]</a> under these ordered cofiber identifications. It identified their components by <a href="#eq:first-roof" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:first-roof">[eq:first-roof]</a> and <a href="#eq:second-roof" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:second-roof">[eq:second-roof]</a> using precisely the stated inverse data. The collected formulas therefore apply to the same $h,F_i,a,Z,t,e$. ◻

</details>

<a id="stmt-auto-remark-1"></a>
<div class="remark">

*Remark 5*. The choices of compatibility homotopy and coherent inverses are part of this realization. [thm:attachment-identification](#thm:attachment-identification) does not claim that the filtration is unique or that its attachments are canonical without those choices.
